2319954.title: Additive Manufacturing in India
2319954.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Additive Manufacturing in India
Building India's Future with Next Generation Digital Manufacturing
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 12:05PM by PIB Delhi

India is emerging as a competitive player in digital revolution through Additive Manufacturing (AM), a 3D printing technology in which digital file controls the process of manufacturing. The National Strategy for Additive Manufacturing (NSAM) is a strategy introduced in 2022 to build India's AM ecosystem. It has made steady progress so far, training over 1,54,000 individuals and supporting 56 AM start-ups. The strategy is now moving into its NSAM 2.0 phase, planning even bigger market than NSAM 1.0 - positioning AM as a building block of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

 

India's Technology Story is Changing Gears

Over the last decade, India has moved from being only a user of technology to becoming a builder of it. Digital public infrastructure has already shown the world how India can build digital systems at population scale. That same confidence is now spreading from the digital world into the physical one - into how India designs, builds and manufactures things. This is where Additive Manufacturing (AM) enters the picture. It is the emerging technology and innovation that is quietly turning digital designs into real, physical objects.

Additive Manufacturing is becoming one of the newest engineering frontiers of India's manufacturing journey. The global AM machines market is projected to touch USD 149 billion by 2035, with the AM-electronics supply chain set to grow from USD 18 billion to USD 112 billion. This gives India a real opening to become a competitive manufacturer of AM platforms across polymers, metals, composites, ceramics and semiconductor-grade materials.

 

Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies

ESTIC-2026, the second edition of India’s Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave, will be held from 27–29 October 2026.The event will be held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, under the theme “Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies.” Organised by the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR), ESTIC-2026 will advance emerging science and technology frontiers. These include Additive Manufacturing (AM) and other emerging technologies with potential for transformative applications. The conclave will catalyse strategic collaborations and support India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.Spanning 12 thematic areas, the event will feature plenary sessions, technical discussions and exhibitions. Read More on Agenda: ESTIC 2026

 

Understanding Additive Manufacturing Technology

AM is not just another manufacturing tool - it is a form of digital engineering that brings in a digital file that completely controls the layer-by-layer material deposition and sometime material composition to build an object. It brings in convergence of computing, electronics, design software and materials science. Every AM object starts out as a digital file, so the technology is closely linked to tools like Computer-Aided Design (CAD), Artificial Intelligence and pattern recognition. AM works on a simple but powerful idea - building an object up, rather than cutting it down. Here is how a digital design turns into a physical object, step by step:

 

  • Virtual design: The process begins with a digital design made in a CAD (Computer-Aided Design) file - either modelled from scratch or captured using a 3D scanner or now a days made using AI from mobile phone photos.
  • STL file: A STL (Standard Tessellation Language) file represents a 3D model as a collection of triangular surfaces. It is one of the commonly used file formats for preparing models for AM. This file instructs what to build to the machine.
  • Slicing: Slicing software divides this digital model into hundreds or thousands of horizontal layers. Once done it instructs machine how to print layer-by-layer.
  • Printing: The sliced file is fed into the AM machine, which reads each layer and builds the object step by step.
  • Additive Process: An AM object is built by laying down successive layers of material until it takes its final shape. Technology evolution has taken digital manufacturing to such accuracies in deposition and composition control that without the digital instructions printing process fails to build properly. Currently there are 40+ such processes in market and R&D stage.
  • Final object: The printer fuses successive layers of material together into a single, complete three-dimensional object. Once printed, post processing is done to make it marketable.

Additive Manufacturing Materials

In myriad applications, the following material categories have been revolutionary in Additive Manufacturing.

  • Thermoplastics:  Thermoplastic polymers are the most popular types of AM materials. Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS), polycarbonate (PC) and polylactic acid (PLA) each offer distinct advantages in different applications. Water-soluble polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) is typically used to create temporary support structures, which are later dissolved away.
  • Metals: Different metals and metal alloys are used in additive manufacturing, which include precious metals like gold and silver to strategic metals like stainless steel and titanium.
  • Ceramics: A variety of ceramics including zirconia, alumina and tricalcium phosphate are also used in additive manufacturing. Also, alternate layers of powdered glass and adhesive are baked together to develop entirely new classes of glass products.
  • Bio Materials: The biomaterials used in AM applications include the hardened material like silicon, calcium phosphate and zinc to support bone structures as new bone growth occurs. The bio-inks fabricated from stem cells are also being explored by researchers to form blood vessels, bladders and many other human organs. Also 3D Printing of human organs such as liver tissues, kidney, heart etc. are being printed using biomaterials and living cells.

 

Reshaping Key Sectors of the Indian Economy

AM is no longer confined to labs and prototypes. It is already being adopted across critical sectors of India's economy and Strategic Sector, backed by government and private players projects on the ground.

Space & Aerospace

India's space programme is embracing additive manufacturing to build lighter, faster hardware. In May 2024, IIT Madras-incubated start-up Agnikul Cosmos launched Agnibaan - SOrTeD, featuring a single-piece, AM printed semi-cryogenic rocket engine. The mission demonstrated how additive manufacturing can enable complex engine designs and support faster, indigenous development of space hardware. NSAM is helping more such start-ups in their R&D for development of critical engine parts using AM.

Defence

The Armed Forces are turning to AM for faster, disaster-resilient construction. The Indian Army inaugurated its first AM-printed two-story dwelling unit at Ahmedabad, built in just 12 weeks, and has since extended the technology to precast defenses in operational terrains like Ladakh. NSAM is supporting all three branches of defense for establishing workshop level facilities for MRO applications.

 

Healthcare

India is building indigenous alternatives to imported medical technology through AM. MeitY has supported AM based medical device manufacturing and startups like OsteoForge that is AM printing natural silk-based implant development under NSAM. The Technology Development Board is supporting 3D-printed bone grafts made from indigenous bioceramic materials. The technology can create grafts customised to a patient’s specific needs and anatomy. It can reduce imports, strengthen domestic medical manufacturing and support more personalised healthcare.

Electronics

India's network of AM centres is building indigenous capability in electronics-grade manufacturing. NSAM has successfully demonstrated AM printed electronics components such as batteries, antennas, varistors, capacitors and many more.  A globally first, IISc has demonstrated Photonic Integrated Circuit blocks using AM printing.

Construction

India is exploring 3D printing as a potential solution for faster and more sustainable construction. The Kelvin 6K Pro, an on-site 3D construction printer, has demonstrated the ability to build 2,500 sq ft homes in under 30 days using low-carbon geopolymer material. The technology has the potential to reduce material and logistics costs, lower carbon emissions and improve construction efficiency. Early applications indicate potential for 30% lower material and logistics costs and 90% lower emissions compared with cement-based construction.

Behind this growing momentum lies a clear government push. Over the past few years, the Centre has moved from isolated pilot projects to a structured, mission-mode approach for Additive Manufacturing -backed by dedicated funding, institutions and a national strategy. NSAM is now developing concrete based supercapacitors for solar energy storage.

Government Policy Initiatives: Building an Indian AM Ecosystem

Recognizing AM as a strategic, next-generation manufacturing technology, the Government of India is building a structured national ecosystem. This effort is anchored in the National Strategy for Additive Manufacturing (NSAM). It is supported by growing national platforms, institutions and initiatives that are strengthening the ecosystem.

 

National Strategy for Additive Manufacturing (NSAM)

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) released the National Strategy for Additive Manufacturing (NSAM) in February 2022. NSAM serves as India’s guiding policy framework for 3D printing and additive manufacturing. Aligned with Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat, the strategy sets clear, time-bound national targets. These targets are being pursued through collaboration among the Centre, States, industry and academia.

The national strategy aims to capture 5% of the global additive manufacturing market and add nearly US$1 billion to India’s GDP. It also targets the development of 50 India-specific additive manufacturing technologies, covering materials, machines, processes and software.

The strategy also seeks to nurture 100 new additive manufacturing start-ups and develop 500 new products. It also aims to train 1 lakh skilled workers for the additive manufacturing workforce. Another objective is to build additive manufacturing capabilities across 10 existing and emerging manufacturing sectors.

To further advance these objectives, the Government has established seven specialised Development and Deployment Centres. These centres support research and development, skilling and hands-on technology access.

 

Did you Know?

The Government of India is nurturing 3D printing skills at the school level through Atal Tinkering Labs (ATLs). Each lab receives a grant of ₹20 lakh to set up dedicated innovation workspaces of 1,200–1,500 sq ft, equipped with Do-it-Yourself (DIY) kits including 3D printers, Robotics, and Internet of Things (IoT). This gives students from Grade VI to Grade XII hands-on exposure to Additive Manufacturing early on - helping build India's future AM workforce from the classroom itself.

 

Progress Under NSAM

More than four years after its launch, the National Strategy for Additive Manufacturing (NSAM) has made steady and measurable progress. Government-supported initiatives have strengthened India’s additive manufacturing ecosystem through skilling, entrepreneurship, technology development and sectoral applications.

More than 1,54, 000 individuals have been trained in additive manufacturing-related skills, creating a growing skilled workforce. Fifty-six additive manufacturing start-ups have also been supported, strengthening India’s innovation and entrepreneurship base. The network of national centres has enabled the development of 65 India-specific technologies including materials, machines, Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM) and printed products. These capabilities are supporting the development of products and prototypes across aerospace, medical devices, electronics, energy, food processing and photonics.

NSAM 2.0

NSAM 2.0 is being conceptualised to support India’s aspiration for AM market acceleration. The next phase plans to accelerate Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) generation, grow AM network through Digital Integration and proposes to develop globally competitive additive manufacturing technologies for commercialization. It aims to improve the affordability of machines and materials through clusters and strengthen the additive manufacturing electronics value chain.

NSAM 2.0 is planning to expand the additive manufacturing start-up base, provide extensive support to Indian defense and promote Sustainable Development Goal (SDG)-driven pilot programmes. It proposes to deepen international cooperation through standards, joint research and technology partnerships. These priorities can strengthen India’s technological capabilities and mainstream additive manufacturing across economic, industrial and societal applications.

National Additive Manufacturing Symposium (NAMS)

NAMS is a national platform for advancing India’s Additive Manufacturing (AM) ecosystem. It brings policymakers, scientists, industry, start-ups, academia and other AM stake holders together on a common platform. The platform promotes coordinated progress across policy, research, innovation and industry.

 

MeitY organised the 2nd NAMS edition on 13 March 2026 in New Delhi. NAMS 2026 strengthened collaboration across India’s AM ecosystem. MoUs were exchanged to deepen ecosystem partnerships, alongside the launch of new AM products. Panel discussions covered NSAM 2.0, defence adoption, industry perspectives and MeitY-supported R&D centres. The symposium also strengthened inter-ministerial coordination on AM applications. State Governments, industry and leading research institutions further strengthened the platform. These efforts highlight the growing relevance of AM across diverse sectors of the Indian economy.

 

Towards a Viksit Bharat

AM is steadily moving from India’s research labs into factories, defence establishments and hospitals. Backed by focused government policies, it is strengthening indigenous manufacturing and reducing reliance on imports. It is also supporting the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat through greater domestic technological capabilities. As India scales its Additive Manufacturing ecosystem, it is creating skilled employment and strengthening its technology base. The technology also supports Industry 5.0 through digital production, advanced automation, distributed and flexible manufacturing. Its applications can further contribute to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through resource efficiency, localised production and sustainable solutions. Together, these efforts position AM as an emerging contributor to India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat.

2319947.title: National Institute of Naturopathy, Pune Invites Applications for BNYS Degree Programme for Academic Session 2026–27
2319947.body_html:
AYUSH
National Institute of Naturopathy, Pune Invites Applications for BNYS Degree Programme for Academic Session 2026–27
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 12:04PM by PIB Delhi

The National Institute of Naturopathy (NIN), Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, has invited applications for admission to the Bachelor of Naturopathy and Yogic Sciences (BNYS) programme for the academic session 2026–27 at its flagship Nisarg Gram campus, Yewalewadi, Pune.

NIN, an autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Ayush, is carrying forward the legacy and vision of Mahatma Gandhi by promoting Naturopathy and Yoga through healthcare, education, training and research. NIN is the first Central Government institution in the country to offer the BNYS programme in affiliation with a Central University, Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University, New Delhi. This marks a significant milestone in strengthening institutional education and academic standards in Naturopathy and Yoga.

The 5½-year full-time residential BNYS programme comprises 4½ years of academic and clinical training, followed by one year of Compulsory Rotatory Residential Internship (CRRI). The programme offers integrated academic education along with extensive clinical exposure in Naturopathy and Yoga. A total of 100 seats are being offered for the academic session 2026–27.

Candidates who have passed 10+2 or an equivalent examination with Physics, Chemistry, Biology (PCB) and English from a recognised Board and fulfil the prescribed eligibility and medical fitness requirements are eligible to apply. Preference will be given to candidates who have appeared for NEET-UG 2026. Any remaining vacant seats will be filled on the basis of 10+2 PCB merit, in accordance with the prescribed admission procedure and reservation norms.

The flagship Nisarg Gram campus, spread over 25 acres, houses a 250-bedded Naturopathy Hospital, academic and research facilities, separate residential hostels for boys and girls, state-of-the-art yoga halls and modern Naturopathy treatment infrastructure. The campus provides an integrated environment for education, clinical training, research and wellness.

The online application process commenced on 29 September 2026 and will close on 19 October 2026 at 5:00 PM. The provisional merit list is scheduled to be released on 27 October 2026, followed by the final merit/waiting list on 30 October 2026. Counselling is scheduled to be conducted on 12–13 November and 18–19 November 2026, while classes are scheduled to commence from 30 November 2026.

The detailed Prospectus, fee structure and application details are available on the NIN website: www.ninpune.ayush.gov.in.

Admission Helpline: +91 7965220180, 9511693564
Email: admission@bnysnin.in

2319900.title: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda to Lead National Launch of JOSH Teams Tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam
2319900.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2319900.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda to Lead National Launch of JOSH Teams Tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam
Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Defence Shri Sanjay Seth and Delhi Chief Minister Smt. Rekha Gupta to Join National Launch of JOSH Teams
JOSH Teams to be Rolled Out Across 55 Districts in 11 States in First Phase to Strengthen Youth-Led Community Mobilisation for TB Mukt Bharat
JOSH Teams to take TB Mukt Bharat Message to Grassroots; Class-I Officers, MY Bharat Volunteers and NCC Cadets to Drive Community Engagement
JOSH Teams to Strengthen Grassroots Participation in India’s TB Elimination Efforts, building on 67,933 Panchayats Across 697 Districts Recognised as TB Mukt in 2025
Initiative Reflects Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Society Approach by Bringing Together Health, Youth and Defence Networks in the Fight Against TB
Posted On: 07 OCT 2026 10:05AM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards further strengthening community participation in India’s fight against tuberculosis (TB), the Union Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, in collaboration with the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports and the Ministry of Defence, will launch JOSH (Joint Squad for Health) Teams on 8 October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. In the first phase, JOSH Teams will be rolled out across 55 districts in 11 States, with the objective of strengthening youth-led community mobilisation and taking the message of TB Mukt Bharat to the grassroots.

Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare and Chemicals & Fertilizers, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, will lead the national launch of JOSH Teams in the presence of Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports; Shri Sanjay Seth, Minister of State for Defence; and Smt. Rekha Gupta, Chief Minister of Delhi. The event will bring together senior leadership and stakeholders from the participating Ministries, elected representatives, Class-I Officers, MY Bharat Volunteers, NCC Cadets and other stakeholders associated with India’s TB elimination efforts.

The programme will feature an achievement video highlighting key milestones of the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, followed by the formal launch of JOSH Teams. New Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials for the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan will also be launched. The event will further witness the launch of Khushi Avatar, an AI-powered chatbot, aimed at strengthening public awareness, community engagement and participation in the national effort towards TB elimination.

Structured Youth Participation for Grassroots TB Mobilisation

JOSH Teams have been envisaged as a structured mechanism to translate the energy and reach of India’s youth into organised community action for TB elimination. The teams will bring together Class-I Officers, MY Bharat Volunteers and NCC Cadets, combining administrative leadership with the extensive youth networks and community outreach capabilities of MY Bharat and NCC.

In the first phase, the initiative will focus on strengthening engagement at the Block/Ward and community levels, taking the TB Mukt Bharat message beyond health facilities and closer to people and communities where they live, work and interact.

Through community outreach and engagement, JOSH Teams will support the dissemination of key messages on TB symptoms, prevention, timely diagnosis and completion of treatment. They will also contribute to efforts to address myths and misconceptions surrounding TB, reduce stigma and encourage individuals, families and communities to participate actively in the national TB elimination movement.

The initiative seeks to enable young people to become active partners in the TB response, providing them with a defined platform to contribute to awareness generation, social mobilisation and community engagement. The convergence of Class-I Officers, MY Bharat Volunteers and NCC Cadets will further strengthen the connect between government programmes and communities at the grassroots.

Building on the Power of Jan Bhagidari

The JOSH Teams initiative builds on the growing emphasis on community participation and Jan Bhagidari as important pillars of India’s TB elimination efforts. In 2025, 67,933 Panchayats across 697 districts were recognised as TB Mukt, reflecting the collective efforts of health workers, elected representatives, community members and volunteers in advancing the national TB elimination agenda.

This achievement underscores the importance of local leadership, community ownership and sustained participation in taking the TB elimination message to the last mile. JOSH Teams will build on this spirit of Jan Bhagidari by harnessing the energy, outreach and social networks of young people to further strengthen awareness, mobilisation and community participation in the TB response.

Whole-of-Government, Whole-of-Society Approach

JOSH Teams represent the Government’s whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to TB elimination by bringing together the institutional strengths and outreach networks of the health, youth and defence sectors.

The Union Ministry of Health & Family Welfare will provide the overall public health and TB elimination framework, while the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports and the Ministry of Defence will facilitate the participation of MY Bharat Volunteers and NCC Cadets, respectively, in community-level mobilisation and outreach.

The initiative reflects the Government’s continued emphasis on convergence across Ministries and sectors, enabling diverse institutional and community networks to contribute towards a common national goal.

The launch of JOSH Teams marks another important step in the Government’s efforts to build a people-centred, participatory and community-driven response to TB, with coordinated action involving Ministries, States and Union Territories, health workers, elected representatives, youth and citizens.

Through stronger grassroots engagement and greater Jan Bhagidari, JOSH Teams will further reinforce the collective resolve to build a TB Mukt Bharat.

2319864.title: ECI Clarifies Protocol for Meetings with Political Delegations, Says No Political Party Sought Appointment Before 4 PM Today
2319864.body_html:
Election Commission
ECI Clarifies Protocol for Meetings with Political Delegations, Says No Political Party Sought Appointment Before 4 PM Today
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 9:44PM by PIB Delhi
  1. Earlier today, during the march of certain political parties towards the Election Commission, it was learnt through the media that some Members of Parliament wished to meet the Commission along with their delegation. With regard to today's developments, it is clarified that, till 4.00 PM today, no political party, through its representatives, had sought an appointment for a meeting with the Election Commission.
  2. Thereafter, at around 4.00 PM, information was received from Delhi Police that a delegation of MPs, led by the Hon'ble Leader of the Opposition, Shri Rahul Gandhi, wished to meet the Commission and submit a memorandum.
  3. In 2025, the Election Commission of India had laid down a procedure for meetings with political parties. All political parties had been informed of the same and they follow this procedure. Whenever a delegation of a political party, or a joint delegation of several parties, wishes to meet the Commission, it seeks an appointment through its duly Authorised Representative. The meeting is thereafter held at a time mutually agreed upon by both sides.
  4. After 4.00 PM today, when the Election Commission was considering the above proposal for the above-mentioned meeting with the Hon'ble MPs, it was informed by the DCP, Delhi Police, that the meeting being sought was to be held with a group of 240 MPs and that the proposed venue was the Parliament House Annexe. The Election Commission considered this request as unusual and therefore, could not be accepted, as, in accordance with ECI protocol, such meetings are held only on the premises of the Election Commission of India.
  5. ECI proposed that its senior-most officer on duty could be sent to the meeting venue to receive the memorandum of the Hon'ble MPs, which in itself would have been an unprecedented step. However, this offer was also declined by the Hon'ble MPs.
  6. ECI respects the parliamentary and democratic processes of the country, as well as its own protocols and conventions, which are of utmost importance. Any political party may, at any time, request for a meeting with the Election Commission; and the Commission, keeping in view the suitability of time, schedules a date and time for the meeting. This is a regular practice.

2319832.title: DRI cracks down on cross-border gold smuggling along Indo-Bangladesh border; seizes over 8.3 kg foreign-origin gold; 4 arrested
2319832.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DRI cracks down on cross-border gold smuggling along Indo-Bangladesh border; seizes over 8.3 kg foreign-origin gold; 4 arrested
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 8:47PM by PIB Delhi

 

 

 


Continuing its sustained crackdown on organised gold smuggling, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has seized around 8.3 kg foreign-origin gold valued at approximately Rs. 12.37 crore in intelligence-led operation in an operation along the Indo-Bangladesh border. Four persons have been arrested in connection with the smuggling activities.

In a significant intelligence led operation DRI officers mounted surveillance along the Indo-Bangladesh border in Cooch Behar District and on 05.10.2026 intercepted four individuals travelling on two motorcycles along the route from the Indo-Bangladesh border at Chowdhurihat to Cooch Behar. A personal search of the suspects led to the recovery of gold biscuits, which were concealed in specially tailored cloth waist belts worn by two of them.

 

A total of 72 gold biscuits, each weighing 116 grams, were recovered from the possession of the said four persons. The total foreign origin gold weighing around 8.3 kg valued at approximately 12.37 crore was seized under relevant provisions of Customs Act, 1962 and all the four persons involved were arrested. Further investigations are underway.

The operation was a culmination of long discreet surveillance done by DRI officials along the Indo-Bangladesh Border in Cooch Behar district. DRI remains steadfast on dismantling organised gold-smuggling networks operating through cross-border corridors. And identifying the wider syndicates behind the movement and distribution of smuggled gold.

LOK SABHA SPEAKER ADDRESSES THE INAUGURAL CEREMONY OF THE SILVER JUBILEE CELEBRATIONS MARKING 25 YEARS OF THE GOA LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY BUILDING
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 8:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Silver Jubilee celebrations programme marking 25 years of the Goa Legislative Assembly Building was inaugurated today by Governor, Goa, Shri Pusapati Ashok Gajapathi Raju. 

Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla emphasised that strong democracies are built on dialogue, diverse views and meaningful public participation. Noting that legislatures are forum for discussion, dialogue, debate and exchange of diverse views, he mentioned that democracy becomes stronger when there is space for agreement as well as disagreement, and when diverse perspectives are brought into the legislative process. India's democratic strength, he said, has been built on the ability of its institutions to accommodate diverse opinions and viewpoints.

Referring to India's growing stature in the global arena, Shri Birla said that India's democratic experience and commitment to constitutional values have strengthened the country's voice in the world. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India is contributing to finding solutions to global challenges while drawing upon the civilisational ethos of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’. He said that the strength of democracy must ultimately be reflected in the manner in which people's expectations and aspirations are translated into policies, laws and effective governance. He also underlined the special responsibility of elected representatives in smaller States such as Goa, where there is close interaction between representatives and citizens. He urged public representatives to remain sensitive to the aspirations, difficulties and challenges faced by their constituents and work towards their timely resolution.

Stressing that technology can significantly enhance public understanding of legislative processes by enabling citizens to access information relating to rules, laws, policies, legislative debates and the work of committees, Lok Sabha Speaker called for greater transparency and accessibility which can deepen the connection between legislatures and the people. Calling for healthy competition among State Legislatures in adopting innovations, Shri Birla said that legislatures should learn from one another and share best practices in areas such as technology, legislative procedures and institutional reforms. The objective, he said, should be to create a “healthy competition” among legislatures to strengthen democratic institutions.

Lok Sabha Speaker also stressed on greater participation of young people in democratic institutions. He said that India's youth are at the forefront of technology, education, research and innovation, and their participation in the legislative process would contribute to the formulation of better policies and laws. He welcomed the initiative of the Goa Legislative Assembly to organise programmes over four days highlighting the history of the Goa Liberation Movement and the legislative journey of the State. Such initiatives, he said, would help connect young people with legislative institutions and enhance their understanding of the democratic process.

Shri Birla mentioned that Goa has a distinctive identity, known not only for its natural beauty, coastline and rich cultural heritage, but also for its harmonious way of life. He congratulated the present and former Chief Ministers, Speakers, Ministers, Members of Parliament and Members of the Goa Legislative Assembly who have contributed to the State's socio-economic development over the past 25 years. He also acknowledged the contribution of all those elected representatives who, through their debates, views and legislative interventions, have strengthened the dignity and prestige of the Assembly. Shri Birla said that Goa's development journey has been distinctive as the State had to simultaneously promote industry, trade, tourism and education while preserving its rich heritage and natural environment. Maintaining this balance, he said, has been a challenging but important responsibility. He noted that Goa has today established a distinct position in the fields of tourism, industry and education, while also maintaining the dignity and quality of life of its people. He appreciated the efforts of successive governments and elected representatives who have contributed to this journey through policies, legislation and public-oriented initiatives.

Shri Birla noted that the Silver Jubilee should not merely be an occasion to celebrate the Assembly's achievements of the past 25 years, but should also provide an opportunity to envision the next 25 years. He urged the Goa Legislative Assembly to prepare a forward-looking roadmap aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat, with maximum participation of citizens, youth and women. He said that every citizen, particularly the person at the last mile, should feel that the Legislative Assembly is a forum that represents and responds to his or her aspirations and expectations. He  emphasised that the next 25 years should focus on making democratic institutions stronger, more accessible, accountable, responsive and results-oriented. Greater public participation in the functioning of legislatures, he said, would make democratic institutions more accountable and responsible towards citizens.

Congratulating the Goa Legislative Assembly on completing 25 years in its present building, Shri Birla expressed confidence that the Assembly would continue to contribute to Goa's economic and social development while preserving its distinctive culture, heritage and natural environment. He conveyed his greetings to all present and former Members, Speakers, Chief Ministers and other public representatives who have contributed to the development of Goa and strengthened the democratic institutions of the State.

On this occasion, Shri Birla released ‘Customised My Stamp and Special Cover with Special Cancellation’ of the Goa Legislative Assembly and Secretariat Building and also felicitated eminent personalities.

Chief Minister, Goa, Shri Pramod Sawant; Speaker, Goa Legislative Assembly, Dr. Ganesh Gaonkar; Minister for Legislative Affairs, Government of Goa, Shri Mauvin Godinho; Leader of Opposition, Goa legislative Assembly, Shri Yuri Alemao and other dignitaries also addressed on the occasion. 

Speaker, Goa Legislative Assembly, Dr. Ganesh Gaonkar delivered the Welcome Address and Deputy Speaker, Goa Legislative Assembly , Shri Joshua Peter De Souza delivered the Words of Gratitude.

2319825.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, MoSJE to Administer Oath to Newly Appointed Members of DWBDNC Governing Body Tomorrow
Shri Narayan Dewasi, Shri Swaroop Singh Banjara to Take Oath as Members of the Board
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 8:40PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and Chairman, Development and Welfare Board for De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Communities (DWBDNC), will administer the oath of office to Shri Narayan Dewasi and Shri Swaroop Singh Banjara, the newly appointed Members of the Governing Body of the Board, in the National Capital tomorrow.

Shri Narayan Dewasi and Shri Swaroop Singh Banjara have been appointed as Members of the Governing Body of DWBDNC by the Department of Social Justice & Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, for a tenure of three years from the date of joining or until further orders, whichever is earlier. Shri Narayan Dewasi assumed charge on 25 September 2026, while Shri Swaroop Singh Banjara assumed charge on 17 September 2026.

The Development and Welfare Board for De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Communities (DWBDNC) works towards addressing the welfare and development concerns of these communities and supporting initiatives aimed at their socio-economic development and empowerment.

The oath-taking ceremony will mark the formal commencement of responsibilities by the newly appointed Members and will further strengthen the Governing Body of DWBDNC in carrying forward its mandate and advancing initiatives for the welfare, socio-economic development and empowerment of De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Communities.

2319822.title: Government appoints Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, PVSM, AVSM, VM, VSM as Chief of the Air Staff (CAS)
2319822.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Government appoints Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, PVSM, AVSM, VM, VSM as Chief of the Air Staff (CAS)
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 8:39PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has appointed Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, PVSM, AVSM, VM, VSM, presently serving as Vice Chief of the Air Staff as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff, in the rank of Air Chief Marshal, with effect from the afternoon of October 31, 2026. The present Chief of the Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh superannuates from office on October 31, 2026.

   

Born on December 09, 1966, Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit was commissioned into the fighter stream of Indian Air Force on December 06, 1986. Prior to assuming charge as the Vice Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Dixit served as Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC) at Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) and Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Central Air Command.

The Air Marshal is an alumnus of National Defence Academy, Defence Services Command & Staff College Bangladesh and National Defence College. He has more than 3500 hours of extensive flying experience on various aircraft including, to name a few, Mirage-2000, variants of MiG, Kiran, Jaguar, IL-78, Hawk and Tejas. He is an Experimental Test Pilot and a Qualified Flying Instructor. During his service career spanning approximately four decades, he has been actively involved in numerous operations and exercises including Op-Safed Sagar, Op-Rakshak and Op-Sindoor.

During his illustrious career, the Air Marshal has held a number of significant field and staff appointments. He commanded a frontline fighter air base in Western Sector and a premier fighter training base in Southern Sector. The operational capability of the Indian Air Force has improved with the contribution of the Air Officer in various capacities. He was awarded Vayu Sena Medal in 2006, Vishisht Seva Medal in 2011, Ati Vishisht Seva Medal in 2023 and Param Vishisht Seva Medal in 2026 in recognition of his exemplary and distinguished service.

2319826.title: Secretary (Labour & Employment) Leads ‘Shram Samvad’ at Rudrapur, Uttarakhand
2319826.body_html:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Secretary (Labour & Employment) Leads ‘Shram Samvad’ at Rudrapur, Uttarakhand
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Labour & Employment, in collaboration with the Labour Department, Government of Uttarakhand, and in association with the Kumaun Garhwal Chamber of Commerce, Entrepreneur Welfare Committee (SEWS-SIDCUL), and SIDCUL Industrial Welfare Association (SSIWA), organized a 'Shram Samvad' - District-Level Capacity Building and Awareness Programme on the Labour Codes at Rudrapur, Uttarakhand. The programme brought together employers and industry stakeholders to strengthen awareness and understanding of the Labour Codes, which came into force on 21 November 2025, and the Central Rules notified on 8 May 2026. The sessions focused on key provisions of the Codes and the compliance requirements applicable to establishments under the new labour law framework.

The programme was presided over by Dr. Chandra Bhushan Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Labour and Employment and brought together around 250 participants from diverse sectors, including employers, industry representatives, HR professionals, legal experts, finance specialists, and other key stakeholders in the labour and employment ecosystem. Officials from Ministry of Labour and Employment, Central Labour Commissioner (Central), Employees' State Insurance Corporation, Employees' Provident Fund Organisation, and Labour Department, Government of Uttarakhand participated in the programme and interacted with the participants.

The programme featured a series of technical sessions designed to provide participants with practical insights into the Labour Codes, employer obligations, and key social security initiatives of the Government of India.

At the outset, Shri Shridhar Babu Adanki IAS, Secretary Labour, Government of Uttarakhand welcomed the participants and set the context for the programme highlighting the importance of collaborative efforts in strengthening labour law compliance. In the keynote address, Dr. Chandra Bhushan Kumar IAS, Secretary, Ministry of Labour & Employment, elaborated on the key provisions of the Labour Codes and emphasized the role of awareness, stakeholder engagement, and capacity building in supporting their smooth and effective implementation. He also highlighted the central schemes Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PMSYM) during the address.

 

Four technical sessions were held, focusing on a comprehensive overview of the Labour Codes, key compliance requirements for employers under the Codes, and on various facets of PMVBRY and PMSYM, respectively.

An interactive Q&A session was also conducted, in which officials from the Ministry and State Government actively participated.

The programme provided a valuable platform for addressing practical implementation challenges and fostering a deeper understanding of the new regulatory framework. The discussions also helped address key concerns of employers and industry stakeholders, while promoting greater clarity on implementation-related issues.

By bringing together government authorities and industry representatives, the programme fostered meaningful dialogue, strengthened stakeholder engagement, and enhanced awareness of the Labour Codes. The exchange of perspectives and practical insights contributed to a better understanding of the new regulatory framework and supported its effective implementation at the grassroots level.

Subsequently, Secretary L&E visited the ESIC hospital Rudrapur and interacted with the Doctors and the Staff He was briefed about the overall functioning of the hospital and facilities available for the Insured Persons. He also suggested several majors for overall improvement in the functioning of the hospital.

2319821.title: IndiaAI Mission Organised AIKosh University Engagement Programme at National Institute of Technology, Andhra Pradesh to Strengthen India's AI Talent Ecosystem
2319821.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
IndiaAI Mission Organised AIKosh University Engagement Programme at National Institute of Technology, Andhra Pradesh to Strengthen India's AI Talent Ecosystem
IndiaAI Mission Deepens Academic Participation through AIKosh University Engagement Programme at NIT Andhra Pradesh
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 8:37PM by PIB Delhi

The IndiaAI Mission, under the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, organised the AIKosh University Engagement Programme (UEP) at the National Institute of Technology, Andhra Pradesh, Tadepalligudem, on October 5, 2026. The programme aimed to strengthen AI awareness, democratise access to AI resources, and equip students with the knowledge and tools required to participate in India's rapidly growing artificial intelligence ecosystem.

Approved by the Government of India in March 2024, the IndiaAI Mission is driving the country's vision of becoming a global leader in artificial intelligence by fostering innovation, enabling responsible AI development, strengthening indigenous AI capabilities, and ensuring that the benefits of AI reach every section of society.

A key pillar of the Mission, AIKosh serves as India's unified data platform, providing access to high-quality datasets, AI models, toolkits, benchmarks and other critical resources that support research and AI application development. Through the AIKosh University Engagement Programme, the IndiaAI Mission seeks to introduce students and academic institutions to these national AI assets while encouraging hands-on learning and innovation.

As part of the programme, 160+ students from NIT Andhra Pradesh participated in expert sessions, live demonstrations and hands-on activities designed to familiarise them with AIKosh and the broader IndiaAI ecosystem. Participants also explored the AIKosh MCP (Model Context Protocol) and AIKosh SDK (Software Development Kit), which enable users to discover datasets and AI models using natural language, simplifying access to national AI resources and lowering barriers for both developers and non-developers.


Speaking on the initiative, Shri Md. Y. Safirulla K IAS, Director, IndiaAI Mission, said: "Guided by the vision of our Honourable Prime Minister to democratize AI, the IndiaAI Mission continues to carry this commitment to campuses across the country. At the National Institute of Technology, Andhra Pradesh, we see the same three pillars that have anchored our work -- People, Planet, and Progress -- brought to life through a new generation of students ready to engage with India's AI ecosystem. The AIKosh University Engagement Programme is how we turn that vision into something tangible: real datasets, real models, and real opportunities for students to contribute to the nation's AI journey."

Welcoming the collaboration, Dr. KV Krishna Rao, Director, NIT Andhra Pradesh, said: "Through the AIKosh platform, we are building a powerful knowledge-transfer system for the nation -- building on foundational efforts like BharatGen. To stay ahead in the global AI race, platforms like AIKosh are essential in harnessing AI to drive positive development for the country."

As part of the next phase of the AIKosh University Engagement Programme, students will be encouraged to contribute datasets through the AIKosh open-source community and the institute's institutional profile on AIKosh. They will also be encouraged to enrich existing datasets and develop proof-of-concept AI applications addressing public-good use cases. Outstanding student-led contributions may be considered for future recognition, creating a pathway from AI literacy and dataset exploration to innovation and real-world problem solving.

The AIKosh University Engagement Programme is a nationwide initiative designed to deepen AI adoption across higher educational institutions by introducing students, researchers and faculty members to India's national AI infrastructure. Today, AIKosh hosts 16,000+ Datasets, 350+ AI models and 200+ use cases, enabling researchers, startups, developers and students to build AI solutions using trusted national resources.

The programme at NIT Andhra Pradesh marks another step towards building a vibrant AI-ready talent pool and advancing the IndiaAI Mission's vision of creating an inclusive, responsible and innovation-driven AI ecosystem for the nation. Through the AIKosh University Engagement Programme, the Mission will continue to engage academic institutions across the country, fostering campus-level AI communities that contribute to datasets, models, applications, research and responsible AI adoption.

2319810.title: PM interacts with Global System for Mobile Communications Association (GSMA) Board Members
2319810.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
PM interacts with Global System for Mobile Communications Association (GSMA) Board Members
Technology must become a tool for inclusive and sustainable development: PM
Technology-driven solutions needed to tackle cyber fraud: PM
Representatives of Telecom companies Applaud India’s Digital Transformation and Growing Global Technology Partnerships
GSMA Board Members Highlight Opportunities for Global Cooperation with India in 6G and AI
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 8:16PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacted with Global System for Mobile Communications Association (GSMA) Board members at Seva Teerth earlier today, ahead of the India Mobile Congress. GSMA is a global organisation unifying the mobile ecosystem, representing mobile operators and organisations across the mobile ecosystem and adjacent industries.

Prime Minister emphasised that technology must become a tool for inclusive and sustainable development. He stressed that democratisation of technology is essential to ensure that no section of society is left behind. He underlined the need to make technology and digital services affordable and accessible, particularly for the Global South, and highlighted the importance of taking technology to the last mile to prevent a widening digital divide.

Prime Minister highlighted the potential of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) as a transformative force, particularly for developing countries. He noted that discussions on DPI with several world leaders had demonstrated its growing global relevance and said that such platforms can serve as a springboard for countries of the Global South.

Addressing the growing challenge of digital and cyber fraud, Prime Minister said the problem requires technology-driven solutions. He suggested sustained awareness messages for users to warn people about potential fraud calls.

Prime Minister also highlighted the need for global standards and common rules for emerging technologies. On the growing threat of deepfakes and AI-generated content, he suggested exploring mechanisms to allow users to immediately identify its origin.

GSMA Board members highlighted India’s emergence as a global leader in digital and mobile connectivity. They noted the rapid expansion of 4G and 5G, the scale of digital public infrastructure and the growth of the telecom and mobile manufacturing ecosystem. They appreciated India’s investment-friendly policy framework and emphasised the role of secure, resilient and trusted digital infrastructure in supporting continued digital growth.

The Board members also highlighted growing opportunities for international cooperation with India in areas including 5G, 6G, AI, cybersecurity, digital inclusion and satellite connectivity.

The meeting was attended by Minister of Communication, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia, Minister of State for Communication, Dr. Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar, GSMA board members  and senior officials of Government of India.

2319801.title: Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 : MoPR and DDWS Take Cleanliness and Waste Management Message to the  Panchayats
2319801.body_html:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj
Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 : MoPR and DDWS Take Cleanliness and Waste Management Message to the  Panchayats
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 8:00PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Panchayati Raj actively observed Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 from 17th September to 2nd October 2026 under the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag; Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”.  In close collaboration with the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), the Ministry issued a Joint Advisory to mobilise all stakeholders, including Panchayati Raj Institutions and Rural Local Bodies, for the successful implementation of the campaign and in furtherance of the Sankalp of ‘Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat’. The key focus areas of SHS-2026 were the Transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) and Clean Public Places; Swachh Paathshala – Yuva for Swachhata; SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir; Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata; and Swachhata se Samriddhi. The DDWS and the Ministry of Panchayati Raj have complementary roles in mobilising rural communities for Swachhata, with Panchayati Raj Institutions playing a central part in drawing out local participation and sustaining its impact through regular sanitation activities. The campaign saw active involvement of the Panchayati Raj Departments of States and Union Territories, Panchayat representatives, functionaries as well as the  citizens.

With the onset of the campaign, Union Minister of Panchayati Raj, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh and the Union Minister of State for Panchayati Raj, Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel reached out to the masses through various mediums spreading the message of the need to imbibe cleanliness as a way of life. Efforts to sensitise citizens about the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2026, also gathered momentum during the campaign. On Swachh Bharat Diwas, 2nd October 2026, Special Gram Sabhas were held across the country alongside the People’s Plan Campaign, Sabki Yojana SabkaVikas wherein all stakeholders were made aware about the SWM Rules, 2026, and plantation drives under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’were taken up. On this occassion, Union Minister of Panchayati Raj, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, participated in the cleanliness drive in Lakhisarai district of Bihar and planted a sapling, calling upon citizens to make cleanliness a part of their daily lives and to become active partners in building a clean, healthy and green India. Earlier as part of the campaign, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Shri (Dr.) Vineet Joshi, administered the Swachhata Pledge to all officers and staff while the Ministry came together for Shramdaan at a public space opposite Prachin Hanuman Mandir, Connaught Place on 1st October 2026 to not just promote cleanliness but also acknowledge the invaluable contribution of Safai Mitras and Safai Karamcharis in making our daily lives smoother by their contributions.

2319800.title: From Waste Picking to Self-Reliance:
2319800.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Waste Picking to Self-Reliance:
Mekala Yesamma’s Journey towards Economic Empowerment
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 7:58PM by PIB Delhi

Financial assistance can play an important role in helping individuals from disadvantaged communities establish sustainable livelihoods and improve their economic condition. Timely support for self-employment can create new income opportunities, strengthen family financial security and promote greater dignity in livelihood.

Ms. Mekala Yesamma, aged 33, belongs to the Scheduled Tribe (ST) community and had been working as a waste picker in the Guntur Municipal Corporation for nearly 12 years. Coming from a financially disadvantaged family, she could not attend school and remained illiterate. Her family faced persistent economic hardships, while limited income and restricted access to opportunities made it difficult for her to meet household needs and secure a better future for her children.

On 19 June 2023, Ms. Yesamma, along with one other member, received financial assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY) of the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation through Navajeevan Organisation. The assistance was provided in the form of capital subsidy for a group project to procure an Open Nallah Cleaner (Tractor-Mounted). The total project cost was Rs. 16,99,952, supported by a loan of Rs. 10,24,964 and capital subsidy of Rs. 6,74,988.

Before receiving the assistance, Ms. Yesamma earned approximately Rs. 8,000 per month through waste-picking activities. With the support provided under the SUY scheme and the resulting livelihood opportunity, she now earns an additional Rs. 10,000 per month, taking her total monthly income to approximately Rs. 18,000. The increase in income has strengthened her ability to meet household expenses, support her children's education and improve the overall standard of living of her family.

The support provided under the SUY scheme has significantly improved Ms. Yesamma’s socio-economic condition and provided her with an opportunity to pursue a more productive and dignified livelihood. The intervention has enhanced her financial security and confidence while reducing her dependence on limited sources of income.

 

 

Expressing her gratitude, Ms. Mekala Yesamma said, "The financial assistance under the SUY scheme has helped me improve my livelihood and increase my monthly income. It has made it easier for me to meet my family’s needs, support my children’s education and work towards a more secure future."

Ms. Mekala Yesamma’s journey demonstrates how timely financial assistance and livelihood support can enable individuals from disadvantaged communities to improve their earning capacity and move towards economic self-reliance. Her experience reflects the role of SUY in creating sustainable livelihood opportunities and promoting dignity, financial security and a stronger, more self-reliant society.

2319793.title: Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia’s Vision and Sustained Efforts Set the Stage for a New Industrial Era in Gwalior
2319793.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia’s Vision and Sustained Efforts Set the Stage for a New Industrial Era in Gwalior
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah to join Bhoomipujan of Asia’s First Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior on 29 October, 2026 at Shri Scindia’s invitation
Shri Scindia’s initiative and sustained efforts are bringing Asia’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone to Gwalior, with 24+ global companies set to participate in the Bhoomipujan together
TMZ has attracted committed investments of over ₹5,500 crore, with the potential to generate 18,000+ employment opportunities
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 7:40PM by PIB Delhi

In a major step towards realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of an Aatmanirbhar Bharat and strengthening India’s telecom manufacturing capabilities, Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia’s initiative and sustained efforts are giving shape to Asia’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ) in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.

The Bhoomipujan ceremony for this landmark project will be held on 29 October 2026, in Gwalior with Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah set to participate. Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah has accepted Shri Scindia’s invitation and confirmed his presence at the ceremony.

Conceived as a transformative industrial initiative for Gwalior, the TMZ is the outcome of Shri Scindia’s sustained engagement with the Department of Telecommunications (Ministry of Communications, Government of India), the Government of Madhya Pradesh and the industry. Shri Scindia’s continued efforts of over 2 years have focused on bringing together the required land, infrastructure, investment and industry participation to translate the idea into a world-class telecom manufacturing ecosystem.

Proposed at the Shrimant Madhavrao Scindia Counter Magnet City (SADA) in Gwalior, the TMZ is envisioned as a major hub for telecom manufacturing, bringing together manufacturing units, technology innovation, research and development, testing and advanced technology capabilities under one ecosystem.

Union Minister Shri Scindia has been personally driving the project through regular reviews and coordination with senior officials of the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh. From identifying and securing land and developing infrastructure to engaging investors and addressing industry requirements, he has maintained sustained focus on taking the project from concept to now execution with the Bhumipujan ceremony on 29 October 2026.

During his recent inspection of the proposed TMZ site in Gwalior, Union Minister Shri Scindia had underlined that the project was not simply an industrial estate, but a strategic opportunity to create a complete telecom manufacturing ecosystem in Gwalior, bringing together more than 24 manufacturing units and companies associated with the telecom sector.

What is the Telecom Manufacturing Zone?

Similar to how a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) functions, Gwalior's Telecom Manufacturing Zone is being developed on a special plug-and-play model. Under this model, companies will have access to ready infrastructure, common facilities and an enabling industrial environment, allowing them to commence manufacturing operations with minimal lead time.

The TMZ will support manufacturing of telecom equipment and components, while also creating capabilities in design, research and development, testing and innovation. The Zone will also provide a platform for industries associated with optical fibre, semiconductors and advanced technologies such as 5G and 6G.

The initiative is aimed at strengthening India’s domestic telecom manufacturing capacity, advancing self-reliance in telecom products and enhancing India’s participation in global manufacturing and technology value chains.

Union Minister Shri Scindia’s Investor Outreach Brings Investment Proposals of Over ₹5,500 Crore. A key pillar of Union Minister Shri Scindia’s efforts has been his direct engagement with investors and industry leaders to bring investment into the Gwalior TMZ.

Proposed entry (artistic rendition) of the TMZ in Counter Magnet City Area, Gwalior

With the objective of attracting leading companies to the project, Shri Scindia led investor engagements and roadshows in Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru, presenting the project’s potential, infrastructure and investment opportunities.

In July 2026, the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh signed an MoU for the establishment of the TMZ. This was followed by investor roadshows led by Shri Scindia and Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav.

The Delhi roadshow resulted in investment commitments of approximately ₹3,500 crore, with the potential to generate around 14,000 employment opportunities. At the Mumbai roadshow held on 4 August, companies expressed commitments of approximately ₹2,000 crore, with the potential to create around 4,000 jobs.

More recently, Shri Scindia convened an investor meeting in Bengaluru with companies from the telecom, electronics, semiconductor and technology sectors. The interaction generated further interest in the project, with additional investment proposals of approximately ₹700–800 crore emerging.

As a result of these sustained efforts, the TMZ has now attracted investment proposals exceeding 5,500 crore, with the potential to generate more than 18,000 employment opportunities.

Union Minister Shri Scindia’s investor outreach has helped position the TMZ as a major catalyst for industrial growth and economic activity across the Gwalior-Chambal region.

Central Government to Provide 100% Financial Support of ₹493 Crore

The Government of India is providing 100% financial assistance of ₹493 crore for the infrastructure development of the first phase of the project. The Government of Madhya Pradesh has made approximately 170 acres of land available free of cost for the project.

For implementation, a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) has been constituted with 51% equity participation by the Government of Madhya Pradesh and 49% by the Department of Telecommunications.

The Centre-State partnership will play a key role in ensuring time-bound implementation, development of industrial infrastructure and provision of essential facilities to investors.

Union Minister Shri Scindia’s Continued Review to Drive Time-Bound Execution

Union Minister Shri Scindia recently conducted a detailed site inspection of the land identified for the TMZ at the Shrimant Madhavrao Scindia Counter Magnet City (SADA), along with senior officials from the Department of Telecommunications and the Government of Madhya Pradesh.

During the visit, he reviewed the progress of the project, land availability, requirements of prospective investors and the roadmap ahead. He directed senior officials to ensure that all project-related work moves forward in a time-bound manner and that the infrastructure and facilities required by investors are put in place without delay.

The project continues to remain among Shri Scindia’s key priorities, with regular reviews being undertaken to ensure that the vision for Gwalior’s telecom manufacturing ecosystem translates into a reality on the ground.

A New Chapter in Gwalior’s Industrial Growth

The proposed Asia’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior, driven by Shri Scindia’s vision and sustained efforts, has the potential to transform the region into a significant hub for telecom manufacturing and technology.

Beyond investment, the project is expected to create new opportunities for local youth in employment, technical skills, innovation and entrepreneurship, while strengthening the industrial ecosystem of Gwalior-Chambal and Madhya Pradesh.

Aligned with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and ‘Make in India, Make for the World’, the TMZ represents a significant step towards establishing India as a global telecom manufacturing hub.

What began as an ambitious vision championed by Shri Scindia is now taking concrete shape on the ground, with major industry participation, significant investment interest and a clear roadmap for execution. The Gwalior Telecom Manufacturing Zone is poised to become a landmark example of Centre-State cooperation, industry-led growth and India’s transition from telecom consumption to telecom manufacturing and global technology leadership.

2319796.title: STRONG DEMOCRACIES ARE BUILT ON DIALOGUE, DIVERSE VIEWS AND MEANINGFUL PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
2319796.body_html:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
STRONG DEMOCRACIES ARE BUILT ON DIALOGUE, DIVERSE VIEWS AND MEANINGFUL PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
TECHNOLOGY AND YOUTH PARTICIPATION CAN GIVE A NEW DIMENSION TO DEMOCRACY: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
LOK SABHA SPEAKER CALLS FOR HEALTHY COMPETITION AMONG STATE LEGISLATURES IN ADOPTING INNOVATIONS
GOA HAS SUCCESSFULLY BALANCED ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT WITH PRESERVATION OF ITS HERITAGE AND NATURAL ENVIRONMENT: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
GOA ASSEMBLY SHOULD PREPARE A 25-YEAR ROADMAP WITH GREATER PARTICIPATION OF YOUTH, WOMEN AND CITIZENS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
LOK SABHA SPEAKER ADDRESSES THE INAUGURAL CEREMONY OF THE SILVER JUBILEE CELEBRATIONS MARKING 25 YEARS OF THE GOA LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY BUILDING
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 7:38PM by PIB Mumbai

Panaji / New Delhi : 6 October 2026


The Silver Jubilee celebrations programme marking 25 years of the Goa Legislative Assembly Building was inaugurated today by Governor, Goa, Shri Pusapati Ashok Gajapathi Raju.  

Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla emphasised that strong democracies are built on dialogue, diverse views and meaningful public participation. Noting that legislatures are forum for discussion, dialogue, debate and exchange of diverse views, he mentioned that democracy becomes stronger when there is space for agreement as well as disagreement, and when diverse perspectives are brought into the legislative process. India's democratic strength, he said, has been built on the ability of its institutions to accommodate diverse opinions and viewpoints.

Referring to India's growing stature in the global arena, Shri Birla said that India's democratic experience and commitment to constitutional values have strengthened the country's voice in the world. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India is contributing to finding solutions to global challenges while drawing upon the civilisational ethos of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’. He said that the strength of democracy must ultimately be reflected in the manner in which people's expectations and aspirations are translated into policies, laws and effective governance. He also underlined the special responsibility of elected representatives in smaller States such as Goa, where there is close interaction between representatives and citizens. He urged public representatives to remain sensitive to the aspirations, difficulties and challenges faced by their constituents and work towards their timely resolution.

Stressing that technology can significantly enhance public understanding of legislative processes by enabling citizens to access information relating to rules, laws, policies, legislative debates and the work of committees, Lok Sabha Speaker called for greater transparency and accessibility which can deepen the connection between legislatures and the people. Calling for healthy competition among State Legislatures in adopting innovations, Shri Birla said that legislatures should learn from one another and share best practices in areas such as technology, legislative procedures and institutional reforms. The objective, he said, should be to create a “healthy competition” among legislatures to strengthen democratic institutions.

Lok Sabha Speaker also stressed on greater participation of young people in democratic institutions. He said that India's youth are at the forefront of technology, education, research and innovation, and their participation in the legislative process would contribute to the formulation of better policies and laws. He welcomed the initiative of the Goa Legislative Assembly to organise programmes over four days highlighting the history of the Goa Liberation Movement and the legislative journey of the State. Such initiatives, he said, would help connect young people with legislative institutions and enhance their understanding of the democratic process.

Shri Birla mentioned that Goa has a distinctive identity, known not only for its natural beauty, coastline and rich cultural heritage, but also for its harmonious way of life. He congratulated the present and former Chief Ministers, Speakers, Ministers, Members of Parliament and Members of the Goa Legislative Assembly who have contributed to the State's socio-economic development over the past 25 years. He also acknowledged the contribution of all those elected representatives who, through their debates, views and legislative interventions, have strengthened the dignity and prestige of the Assembly. Shri Birla said that Goa's development journey has been distinctive as the State had to simultaneously promote industry, trade, tourism and education while preserving its rich heritage and natural environment. Maintaining this balance, he said, has been a challenging but important responsibility. He noted that Goa has today established a distinct position in the fields of tourism, industry and education, while also maintaining the dignity and quality of life of its people. He appreciated the efforts of successive governments and elected representatives who have contributed to this journey through policies, legislation and public-oriented initiatives.

Shri Birla noted that the Silver Jubilee should not merely be an occasion to celebrate the Assembly's achievements of the past 25 years, but should also provide an opportunity to envision the next 25 years. He urged the Goa Legislative Assembly to prepare a forward-looking roadmap aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat, with maximum participation of citizens, youth and women. He said that every citizen, particularly the person at the last mile, should feel that the Legislative Assembly is a forum that represents and responds to his or her aspirations and expectations. He  emphasised that the next 25 years should focus on making democratic institutions stronger, more accessible, accountable, responsive and results-oriented. Greater public participation in the functioning of legislatures, he said, would make democratic institutions more accountable and responsible towards citizens.

Congratulating the Goa Legislative Assembly on completing 25 years in its present building, Shri Birla expressed confidence that the Assembly would continue to contribute to Goa's economic and social development while preserving its distinctive culture, heritage and natural environment. He conveyed his greetings to all present and former Members, Speakers, Chief Ministers and other public representatives who have contributed to the development of Goa and strengthened the democratic institutions of the State.

On this occasion, Shri Birla released ‘Customised My Stamp and Special Cover with Special Cancellation’ of the Goa Legislative Assembly and Secretariat Building and also felicitated eminent personalities.

Chief Minister, Goa, Shri Pramod Sawant; Speaker, Goa Legislative Assembly, Dr. Ganesh Gaonkar; Minister for Legislative Affairs, Government of Goa, Shri Mauvin Godinho; Leader of Opposition, Goa legislative Assembly, Shri Yuri Alemao and other dignitaries also addressed on the occasion.  

Speaker, Goa Legislative Assembly, Dr. Ganesh Gaonkar delivered the Welcome Address and Deputy Speaker, Goa Legislative Assembly , Shri Joshua Peter De Souza delivered the Words of Gratitude.

2319792.title: The Many Expressions of Karnataka in the 8th Edition of PM Mementos
2319792.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
The Many Expressions of Karnataka in the 8th Edition of PM Mementos
30 mementos from Karnataka in the PM Mementos e-auction showcase its diverse traditions, crafts, cultural heritage and contemporary achievements.
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 7:35PM by PIB Delhi

The Karnataka collection at the 8th edition of PM Mementos is a testament of diversity of India’s artistic and cultural heritage not only across India but also within the state itself.

The collection brings together distinct expressions of Karnataka’s cultural landscape.

The memento of Goddess Saradamba who is considered an incarnation of Saraswati represent Sringeri’s long-standing association with knowledge and devotion, while the artefacts associated with Sant Sevalal reflect the spiritual and cultural identity of the Banjara community.

The Kinnal art and Bidriware pieces highlight Karnataka’s rich tradition of craftsmanship, while the photo print of the Kambala Festival captures a living rural tradition. The Mysore Peta and other ceremonial turbans add another layer, reflecting traditions of identity, honour and celebration.

 

The collection also captures a Karnataka that is rooted in its heritage yet firmly connected to the present. The signed badminton racket of Paralympic medallist Suhas Yathiraj, alongside contemporary artworks and a replica scale model of the Sri Madhusudan Sai Institute of Medical Sciences and Research, brings present day achievements into the conversation.

Taken together, the 30 mementos offer more than a collection of objects from Karnataka. They offer a glimpse of the many cultural worlds that exist within one state and, in doing so, reflect the larger richness of India’s diversity. The PM Mementos auction becomes a platform where these varied expressions of India can be brought together, preserved and shared beyond the moment for which they were created or presented.

The 8th edition of PM Mementos is currently live and has been extended until 31 October 2026. Proceeds from the auction will support the Namami Gange Project.

Interested bidders can place their bids online through the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal: https://pmmementos.gov.in
