2319791.title: Ministry Of Culture Successfully Organizes “Swachhata Hi Seva” Campaign 2026 (17th September - 2nd October 2026)
2319791.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Ministry Of Culture Successfully Organizes “Swachhata Hi Seva” Campaign 2026 (17th September - 2nd October 2026)
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 7:35PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Culture celebrated the nationwide Swachhta Hi Seva (SHS) campaign 2026 from 17th September to 2nd October 2026 by organizing a series of cleanliness, awareness and community participation activities across its 43 organizations and cultural institutions. This year’s theme was “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag: Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”.

The campaign witnessed a wide range of activities undertaken by the Ministry’s organizations and field institutions, including transformation of Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs), Shramdaan drives, awareness programmes, Waste-to-Art initiatives and thematic art competitions. These initiatives focused on waste segregation, reduction of single-use plastics, principles of Reduce, Reuse and Recycle (3Rs), and environmental conservation.

Through these initiatives, the Ministry of Culture and its organizations promoted a culture of cleanliness, environmental responsibility and Jan Bhagidari, while linking the objectives of Swachhata with the Ministry’s wider mandate of culture and heritage. The activities encouraged officers, staff, students, artists and local communities to contribute actively towards cleaner, healthier and more sustainable public spaces.

The key achievements of the campaign are as under:

  1. 424 Cleanliness Target Units (CTUs) were identified & transformed and 128 public places were identified & cleaned with active contribution of more than 10,000 participants.
  2. 207 Nukkad Nataks were organized by Zonal Cultural Centres, National School of Drama, Sangeet Natak Akademi and Centre for Cultural Resources & Training, through their regional offices, at various locations across the country, including schools, colleges, and other prominent public places with high footfall.
  3. The Archaeological Survey of India, Ministry of Culture through its regional circles conducted Cleanliness drives across various monuments and office premises. Driven by Jan Bhagidari, ASI officials and local volunteers performed Shramdaan to remove plastic waste, dry leaves, and littered garbage from monument pathways, lawns, and central areas. Plantation drives were also conducted at selected Monuments in which more than 300 trees were planted.
  4. Lalit Kala Akademi, Ministry of Culture organized Waste to Wealth camps on themes “Kabaad se Jugaad” & “Kabaad se Kala” across its regional centres. These camps brought together local sculptors, women artists and students to transform waste materials into creative artworks, thereby promoting recycling, environmental awareness and sustainable art practices.
  5. The National Science Centre, Delhi organized a similar two-day workshop on Waste to Art (30th September – 1st October 2026) to promote the concept of recycling and creative use of waste materials involving school students.
  6. Under the "Swachh Pathshala: Youth for Cleanliness" theme, the Ministry's organizations conducted art competitions and awareness programmes for school and college students, along with 178 demonstration activities and Jal Sanchay Samvad sessions that drew over 2,500 students.
  7. Slogan-Writing & Poster Making Competitions on themes “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag” & “Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat” were organized at Kartavya Bhavan 2, New Delhi with enthusiastic participation from officers & staff of the Ministry.
  8. A Shramdaan Drive was organized at the premises of the National Archives of India, New Delhi on 29th September, 2026 with enthusiastic participation from officers & staff of the Ministry.
  9. On the occasion of Swachh Bharat Diwas (2nd October 2026), a Shramdaan & Plantation Drive led by Secretary (Culture) was organized at Purana Quila, New Delhi with active participation from officers & staff of the Ministry. Sanitation kits were also distributed to Swachhata Mitras during this event.
  10. Five Safai Mitra Suraksha Shivirs were organized, during which Safai Mitras across the Ministry’s organizations were enrolled as beneficiaries under various Government schemes.
  11. The Swachhta Pledge was administered across organizations of the Ministry, reaffirming the collective commitment towards cleanliness, hygiene and responsible civic participation.

The campaign strengthened the culture of cleanliness and hygiene across cultural institutions, heritage sites and public spaces, while raising awareness about environmental sustainability and reinforcing Jan Bhagidari in building a clean, green and sustainable Bharat. The campaign was further amplified through various social media platforms, with more than 200 posts generating over 370K views and significant audience engagement. #SwachhtaHiSeva #CultureForCleanliness.

Ministry of Defence
Government appoints Air Marshal Ashutosh Dlxit, PVSM, AVSM, VM, VSM as Chief of the Air Staff (CAS)
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 6:38PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has appointed Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, PVSM, AVSM, VM, VSM, presently serving as Vice Chief of the Air Staff as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff, in the rank of Air Chief Marshal, with effect from the afternoon of October 31, 2026. Thepresent Chief of the Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singhsuperannuates office on October 31, 2026.

Born on December 09, 1966, Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit was commissioned into the fighter stream of Indian Air Force on December 06, 1986. Prior to assuming charge as the Vice Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Dixit has served as Chief of Integrated Defence Staff to the Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee (CISC) at Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) and Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Central Air Command.

The Air Marshal is an alumnus of National Defence Academy, Defence Staff Service College (Bangladesh) and National Defence College. He has more than 3500 hours of extensive flying experience on various aircrafts including to name a few; Mirage-2000, variants of Mig, Kiran, Jaguar, IL-78, HAWK and Tejas. He is an Experimental Test Pilot and a Qualified Flying Instructor. During his service career spanning approximately four decades, he has been actively involved in numerous operations and exercises including Op-Sated Sagar, Op-Rakshak and Op Sindoor.

During his illustrious career, the Air Marshal has held a number of significant field and staff appointments. He commanded a front-line fighter air base in Western Sector and a premiere fighter training base in Southern Sector. The operational capability of Indian Air Force has improved with contribution of the Air Officer in various capacities. He was awarded Vayu Sena Medal in 2006, Vishisht Seva Medal in 2011, AtiVishisht Seva Medal in 2023 and Param Vishisht Seva Medal in 2026 in recognition of his exemplary and distinguished service.

2319761.title: Ministry of Coal holds Special Drive with focus on E-waste Management as part of Special Campaign 6
2319761.body_html:
Ministry of Coal
Ministry of Coal holds Special Drive with focus on E-waste Management as part of Special Campaign 6
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 6:31PM by PIB Delhi

In accordance with the guidelines of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) regarding Special Campaign 6, Ministry of Coal has held a special drive with focus on E-Waste Management across all the coalfield offices on 6th October, 2026. 2152 employees across 74 field offices participated in this special drive.

A one-day workshop on “E-Waste Management” chaired by Joint Secretary Shri Sanjeev Kumar Kassi, was held at the Ministry of Coal (MoC) Conference Room in hybrid mode. Ms. Riya Soni, Scientist-B, CPCB, MoEFCC, made a presentation on e-waste management, covering key aspects of responsible e-waste handling and management.

 

The workshop aimed to sensitize officials of the Ministry of Coal and its Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) on the critical need for systematic segregation and proper disposal of electronic waste (e-waste).

This workshop was attended by Senior officials from the Ministry who attended the workshop in person, while officials from Coal India Limited (CIL) and its subsidiaries, NLC India Limited (NLCIL), Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL), Coal Controller’s Organisation (CCO), and the Coal Mines Provident Fund Organisation (CMPFO) participated virtually.

Quiz Competition at CCO:

The Coal Controller's Organization (CCO) office in Delhi organized a quiz competition on the theme of 'E-Waste Management.

 

E-Waste Kiosk:

In line with the overarching theme of Special Campaign 6, E-Waste Collection Workstations (E-Waste Kiosk) to facilitate systematic collection, segregation, and responsible disposal of electronic waste at the ground level were held at various field offices.

2319749.title: Chintan Shivir 2026 Concludes with Focus on Collaborative Knowledge Sharing for Quality Road Infrastructure
2319749.body_html:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
Chintan Shivir 2026 Concludes with Focus on Collaborative Knowledge Sharing for Quality Road Infrastructure
Two-day conclave provides platform for Centre, States and stakeholders to share experiences, best practices and practical solutions
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 6:20PM by PIB Delhi

The two-day “Chintan Shivir 2026 – A National Conclave on Highway Infrastructure” concluded today at Statue of Unity, Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, with a renewed focus on strengthening Centre-State collaboration, sharing field-level experiences and building institutional capacity for delivery of quality road infrastructure.

In his valedictory address, Secretary, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Shri V. Umashankar, said the Chintan Shivir has provided an opportunity to create a common community of the highways and road sector, enabling States and other stakeholders to share initiatives, experiences and solutions at the policy as well as implementation levels.

Shri Umashankar highlighted that the focus of infrastructure development is increasingly shifting towards quality, with the vision of Viksit Bharat requiring high-quality roads across urban and rural areas, State Highways, National Highways and Expressways.

A key outcome of the deliberations was the opportunity for States to leverage technology platforms and institutional capabilities developed at the national level. Platforms such as PM GatiShakti, Data Lake, eDAR, contractor rating systems and Bhoomi Rashi can be made available for State-level applications, with technical handholding and capacity-building support.

The AI-enabled eDAR platform, currently being used for the National Highway network, can also support States in analysing accident patterns on State and local roads and developing evidence-based interventions for improving road safety, subject to availability of relevant road data.

The deliberations also highlighted the need to strengthen the construction ecosystem through professionalisation, skill development and improved supervision. Shri Umashankar emphasised the importance of focused skill development and capacity building among construction workers to enhance construction practices and ensure better quality outcomes.

Emphasis was also placed on strengthening the quality-based selection and performance assessment of DPR consultants, Authority Engineers and Independent Engineers, with greater weightage to technical capability and past performance. These measures are aimed at addressing gaps in supervision and ensuring better project outcomes.

The conclave further discussed the scope for States to adopt innovative contracting and financing mechanisms, including Model Concession Agreements, BOT and Annuity-based models, particularly for the development of State Highways and State Expressways. The experience and expertise developed at the national level can be utilised by States through structured handholding and capacity-building.

Shri Umashankar also invited States to organise their own Chintan Shivirs and workshops, with participation from domain experts and officers to facilitate knowledge exchange and wider adoption of successful practices.

The two-day conclave featured thematic sessions on PM GatiShakti and integrated infrastructure planning; Land Acquisition and Bhoomi Rashi; Model Concession Agreements and Ratings; Designing Safe Highways, Green Highways, Road Safety and Toll Reform; and Quality Assurance and Project Monitoring.

The sessions facilitated Centre-State dialogue, exchange of best practices and identification of practical and replicable solutions to implementation challenges, reinforcing a collaborative approach towards building future-ready, safe and high-quality road infrastructure in the country.

2319744.title: From Addiction To Independence
2319744.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Addiction To Independence
Thoubal, Manipur’s L. Delay Rebuilds His Life Through ODIC Support
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi

Timely counselling, medical assistance, rehabilitation and family support can play an important role in helping individuals overcome substance dependence, rebuild their confidence and return to productive livelihoods. Targeted intervention can also help beneficiaries restore family relationships, develop a disciplined lifestyle and move towards greater social and economic self-reliance.

At the age of 24, L. Delay (name changed), an OBC beneficiary from Thoubal, Manipur, was struggling with alcohol dependence that had gradually affected his education, family relationships and emotional well-being. He began consuming alcohol after completing Class 12, initially under peer pressure. Over time, occasional consumption developed into a serious dependence, with alcohol becoming a daily necessity. His addiction had a significant impact on his education and family life. Frequent quarrels at home and the stigma associated with his condition further deepened his distress.

Following a family conflict, L. Delay left home and began staying with his close relative in Bishnupur district. Recognising his need for professional assistance, he was brought by his relative to the nearby Outreach and Drop In Centre (ODIC), Nambol Phoijing Makha, Bishnupur District, Manipur, where he received timely support and rehabilitation.

The ODIC provided L. Delay with a comprehensive package of support, including home detoxification, medical assistance, psychological counselling, behavioural rehabilitation and family counselling. He was also provided guidance to strengthen his ability to resist peer pressure, along with vocational support and assistance in rebuilding his social and family relationships. The structured intervention enabled him to address the underlying challenges associated with his alcohol dependence while gradually restoring his confidence and sense of purpose.

Over a period of three months of structured intervention and continued support, L. Delay successfully recovered from alcohol dependence. The counselling and rehabilitation process helped him develop a more disciplined lifestyle and make a firm commitment to remain free from alcohol. Continued family support also played an important role in helping him regain stability and reconnect with his responsibilities.

Today, L. Delay is working as a salesman at a large store in Kakching Bazar, earning a stable salary and contributing to his household. From a period marked by financial instability, family conflict and alcohol dependence, he has moved towards productive employment, financial independence and a more stable life.

L. Delay’s journey demonstrates how timely intervention, counselling, medical care, family support and vocational rehabilitation can help individuals overcome substance dependence and return to mainstream social and economic life. His experience reflects the importance of accessible rehabilitation services in enabling individuals to rebuild their lives with discipline, dignity and renewed purpose.

2319740.title: Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth to inaugurate SAREX-2026 off Paradip coast
2319740.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth to inaugurate SAREX-2026 off Paradip coast
Indian Coast Guard to also host 24th NMSAR Board Meeting at Bhubaneswar
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth will inaugurate the 12th National Maritime Search & Rescue Exercise (SAREX-2026) on 07 October 26, and witness SAR Demo off Paradip coast on 08 October 26 being organized by the Indian Coast Guard. A key highlight of this exercise is the international participation of 32 observers from 30 countries, underscoring the cooperative protocols, strategic importance, and global interoperability of the drill.

SAREX-2026 will be one of the largest and most complex SAR exercises ever conducted in the region, deploying 15 Coast Guard ships, two Dornier aircraft, three Advanced Light Helicopters, a Chetak helicopter, IAF C-130J and Mi-17 aircraft, two Indian Navy ships, civil/state assets, and shore-based support units.

The exercise will simulate a Mass Rescue Operation involving concurrent aeronautical and maritime distress situations; including ditching of a passenger aircraft at sea with 228 persons onboard and its impact with container vessel MV Zumba.

The Indian Coast Guard will also convene the 24th National Maritime Search & Rescue (NMSAR) Board Meeting at Bhubaneswar under the Chairmanship of Director General Paramesh Sivamani, Director General, Indian Coast Guard. Deliberations will focus on strengthening national SAR preparedness, enhancing distress-alert management, and ensuring faster mobilisation of rescue assets through technology integration and seamless inter-agency coordination.

The 24th NMSAR Board Meeting and SAREX-2026 highlight India's resolve to build a faster, technology-enabled and internationally connected SAR framework, in consonance with the vision of SAGAR and the spirit of MAHASAGAR.

2319721.title: PM Mementos Brings Sikkim’s Cultural Heritage Closer to Citizens
2319721.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
PM Mementos Brings Sikkim’s Cultural Heritage Closer to Citizens
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi

The 8th edition of PM Mementos, beyond its noble cause of supporting the Namami Gange initiative, offers citizens an opportunity to connect with and own a piece of India’s diverse cultural heritage.

Among the mementos up for auction in this edition are two distinctive artefacts from Sikkim that offer a glimpse into the unique artistic heritage of the state. The inclusion of these artefacts places Sikkim’s heritage on a national platform, allowing objects that were once part of a ceremonial exchange to find a new connection with citizens and collectors.

 

 

One of the featured pieces is a finely crafted brass sculpture of Lord Buddha, which was gifted to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi by the Governor of Sikkim. The second artefact is a Tibetan Buddhist tabletop prayer wheel, or Mani Khorlo, embossed with the sacred “Om Mani Padme Hum” mantra, reflecting the artistic and spiritual ethos of the Himalayan state.

The presence of these two artefacts in this year’s auction speaks to the diversity of India’s cultural landscape. It also highlights the important role that initiatives such as PM Mementos can play as a unifying force, bringing the country’s diverse cultural traditions closer to its citizens.

The 8th edition of PM Mementos is currently live and has been extended until 31 October 2026. Proceeds from the auction will support the Namami Gange Project. Interested bidders can place their bids online through the official PM Mementos e-Auction portal: https://pmmementos.gov.in

2319703.title: Asian Games 2026
2319703.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Asian Games 2026
India's Journey from New Delhi to Aichi-Nagoya
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 5:33PM by PIB Delhi

Asian Games 2026 at a Glance

The Asian Games, also known as Asiad, are the biggest sports competition in Asia, held once every four years. They are organized by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) and currently have 45 participating countries or regions. The 20th Asian Games were held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from September 19 to October 4, 2026. The official slogan was “Imagine One Asia.” This is the third time that Japan has hosted the Asian Games, following the earlier editions held in Tokyo (1958) and Hiroshima (1994).

This major event was spread over 16 days of intense world-class competitions. It featured 43 sports and 71 disciplines in a grand showcase of athletic excellence. A total of 1,407 medals were awarded across 469 exciting events during the Games.

Alongside the Asian Games, Japan also hosting the 5th Asian Para Games from October 18 to October 24, 2026, in Aichi-Nagoya. This marks the first time Japan has hosted the Para Games.

Understanding the Asian Games 2026 Emblem

The colour and design of the official emblem combine local and cultural significance with dynamics of sports. While the curves represent liveliness, the purple, gold, and green centre lines evoke the image of people uniting and advancing towards a bright red sun-the official symbol of the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA). Purple represents Aichi’s prefectural flower, the iris; gold symbolizes Kinshachi, the iconic golden tiger-fish roof ornaments of Nagoya Castle; and green reflects the strong environmental consciousness of Aichi-Nagoya, fostered through landmark events such as EXPO 2005 Aichi, COP10, and the UNESCO World Conference on ESD. The emblem contains the first letters of Asia, Aichi and Nagoya initials: “A” is depicted in the purple curve and centre line, “N” in purple and gold.

 

Asian Games 2026 Official Mascot

“HONOHON,” the mascot of the 20th Asian Games, represents the fiery passion of athletes.  The name is derived from the Japanese word ‘honoho’, connected to the origin of the Japanese word for flame. It’s design is inspired by the Shachihoko, one of the distinctive symbols of the Nagoya Castle and guarding deity of Aichi-Nagoya.

 

First Asian Games in 1951: India’s Founding Role

India's connection with the Asian Games goes back to the very beginning, when the first edition was held in New Delhi in 1951. This was done against the backdrop of post-World War II efforts to strengthen ties among Asian nations, with several regions of Asia having been recently decolonized. The idea of an Asian sporting competition was mooted by India as a means to display unity and rebuild the bonds between Asian nations that the war had broken. The idea of the Asian Games was first conceived by Prof. G.D. Sondhi, a member of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) for India. The suggestion for holding the Asian Games was first made at a conference of Asian Countries held in New Delhi in 1947, and it was decided to call it the Asian Games.

The inaugural Asian Games were held in New Delhi in March, 1951. President Rajendra Prasad declared them open at the National Stadium. Eleven nations sent 489 athletes to compete across six sports at that first edition. India finished second in the medal table that year, behind Japan. Since then, the Games have become a big event that fosters friendship through sports and contributes to world peace by recognizing diversity.

India's Contingent at Aichi-Nagoya 2026

India fielded one of its largest-ever multi-sport delegations at the Asian Games 2026, with a 501-athlete contingent across 36 sporting disciplines. More than 300 athletes in the contingent were making their Asian Games debut.

A grand send-off ceremony was held in New Delhi on 8 September 2026, ahead of the team’s departure. Union Minister Dr Mandaviya, Indian Olympic Association (IOA) President Dr P.T. Usha and Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav attended the event, and the official contingent jersey was unveiled. The Indian Olympic Association organised the event.

Dr. Mandaviya (Centre), along with IOA President Dr. P.T. Usha (right) & Secretary (Sports) Hari Ranjan Rao (left), unveiled the official contingent jersey ahead of the Asian Games 2026.

Image Source: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

At the opening ceremony on 19 September 2026, double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker and Kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat led India's parade.

India's Gold Medal Triumph at Aichi-Nagoya 2026

India’s campaign at the 2026 Asian Games was highlighted by a 21-gold-medal haul, anchored by strong performances across precision events and team sports. Archery led the gold tally with 5 titles, supported by Shooting and Boxing, which each won 3 gold medals. In team sports, India executed a sweeping "gold rush" across Cricket, Hockey, and Kabaddi, securing 2 gold medals in each sport. Standout performances included the men's cricket team defeating Pakistan by 19 runs in the final, the men's hockey team retaining their continental title with a resounding 5-1 victory over Malaysia, and double gold victories across both the men's and women's kabaddi competitions. Further gold medals in Wrestling (2), Athletics (1) and Golf (1) brought India’s total to 21, reflecting the country’s strong and diverse performance across the continental sporting arena.

India's Participation in the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games

The Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games will be held in Japan from 18 to 24 October 2026. Around 3,000 athletes from 45 National Paralympic Committees across Asia are expected to compete at these Games. The Games will feature eighteen Para sports.

India will participate through the Paralympic Committee of India, its recognised National Paralympic Committee for the Games. This will mark India's fifth appearance at the Asian Para Games, following its record 111-medal haul including 29 Gold medals at Hangzhou 2022 Asian Para Games. Out of the 111 medals, female athletes contributed 40 medals (36% of the medal tally). Previously, India had won 14 medals in the 2010 edition, 33 in 2014 and 72 in 2018.

 

From Grassroots to Global Podiums: India's Policy Push for Sports

 

Khelo Bharat Niti

The Government launched Khelo Bharat Niti, India's national sports policy, on 1 July 2025. It seeks to build a strong, inclusive, and performance-driven sports system. It focuses on bridging the rural-urban gap in training and facilities. It stresses community participation and partnerships to reduce training costs. The policy sets its sights on excellence at the 2036 Olympics. It links sports with school education under the National Education Policy 2020. It also supports women, tribal communities, and persons with disabilities.

Record Financial Support

The Union Budget 2026-27 allocated a record ₹4,479.88 crore to the sports ministry. This is up from ₹1,219 crore in 2013-14.  The Cabinet has also approved a revamped Khelo India scheme for 2026-27 to 2030-31. With support to National Sports Federations, the combined outlay is ₹36,441 crore. Khelo India alone received ₹924.35 crore for 2026–27. Earlier, the scheme had a ₹3,790.50 crore outlay for 2021–22 to 2025–26. The Budget also earmarked ₹500 crore for sports goods manufacturing.

Finding Talent Early

Khelo India is the flagship programme for grassroots sport. By July 2026, it had set up 1,067 Khelo India Centres. It has approved 349 new sports infrastructure projects worth ₹3,176 crore. It supports 2,745 Khelo India Athletes with coaching, equipment, medical care, and a monthly allowance. More than 63,000 athletes have competed in the Khelo India Games since 2018.

The Khelo India Rising Talent Identification (KIRTI) initiative identifies and nurtures talent among children aged 9 to 18 years. Its 174 Talent Assessment Centres use data tools for fair, merit-based selection.

Backing Top Athletes

The Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) supports India's athletes. It supports athletes through foreign training, international competitions, coaching camps, and specialised equipment. Athletes receive a monthly stipend of ₹50,000. Junior athletes in the Development Group receive ₹25,000 a month. As of April 2026, TOPS supports 55 Core Athletes, 62 Para Core Athletes and 140 Development Athletes; in addition, 67 core athletes are in hockey. TOPS played an important role in India's medals at the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Olympic Games.

Education, Fitness and Fair Play

The National Sports University in Imphal was established in 2018. It offers education in sports science, technology, management and coaching.

The Fit India Movement encourages people to make fitness part of daily life. Parliament passed the National Sports Governance Bill in August 2025. It provides for a National Sports Board to recognise sports bodies. A National Sports Tribunal will settle sports disputes.

Beyond Aichi-Nagoya: India's Long Olympic Road

Aichi-Nagoya 2026 sits within India's broader roadmap toward the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and beyond. More than three hundred of India's five-hundred-plus athletes are making their Asian Games debut this year. This scale of debutant participation reflects the growing depth and expanding bench strength of Indian sport today.

The government has also outlined a ten-year plan investing over ₹36,000 crore to strengthen sports infrastructure nationwide. This investment aims to firmly establish India on the global sporting stage well before 2036. The Sports Ministry has called for a coordinated 360-degree approach involving federations, states and other stakeholders.

India's 85-medal campaign at Aichi-Nagoya, including 21 gold medals, marks another significant chapter in the country's sporting journey. With strong performances across traditional strengths and emerging disciplines, the Games have added further momentum to India's preparations for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and its longer-term sporting ambitions.

2319709.title: COAS FLAGS IN JOINT INDO-ARGENTINE ARMY MOUNTAINEERING EXPEDITION IN NEW DELHI
2319709.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
COAS FLAGS IN JOINT INDO-ARGENTINE ARMY MOUNTAINEERING EXPEDITION IN NEW DELHI
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 5:33PM by PIB Delhi

General Dhiraj Seth, Chief of the Army Staff (COAS), today flagged in members of the Joint Indo-Argentine Army Mountaineering Expedition in New Delhi, following their successful ascent of Mt Abi Gamin (7,355 metres) on 17 September and Mt Kamet (7,756 metres) on 21 September 2026. Mt Kamet located in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand is the third-highest peak in India after Mt Kanchenjunga and Mt Nanda Devi.

The 35-member expedition, led by Lieutenant Colonel Chirag Chatterjee, comprising 25 personnel of the Indian Army and 10 personnel of the Argentine Army was flagged off from the Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi, on 21 August 2026. Operating in demanding Himalayan conditions, the mountaineers negotiated extreme cold, high winds, snowfields, steep rock sections, crevasses and other challenges of high-altitude terrain to summit both peaks. The achievement reflects their physical endurance, technical proficiency, mental resilience and close coordination.

The expedition is the third joint mountaineering venture between the two Armies, following earlier two expeditions to Mt Aconcagua (6,962 metres) in Mendoza, Argentina, in January 2025 and Mt Kun (7,077 metres) in the Suru Valley, Ladakh, in August 2025.

These successive expeditions have strengthened professional cooperation, interoperability, camaraderie and mutual trust between the Indian and Argentine Armies, while providing the valuable experience of operating together in demanding high-altitude environments.

2319696.title: Secretary, DFS, Shri Sanjay Lohiya chairs review meeting on progress of Financial Inclusion Schemes with senior executives of Public Sector and Private Sector Banks
2319696.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Secretary, DFS, Shri Sanjay Lohiya chairs review meeting on progress of Financial Inclusion Schemes with senior executives of Public Sector and Private Sector Banks
Banks urged to enhance digital outreach and focus on end-to end digital processing of loans during the meeting
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 5:23PM by PIB Delhi

The Secretary, Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance, Sh. Sanjay Lohiya  chaired a review meeting with heads of all Public Sector Banks (PSBs) and Executive Directors of major Private Sector Banks (PVBs), in New Delhi today. The review meeting was also attended by senior officials of Department of Financial Services.

During the meeting, a detailed review of the progress under various Financial Inclusion schemes including Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), Atal Pension Yojana (APY), Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY), Stand Up India, PM Street Vendor's Atma Nirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi), PM Vishwakarma, PM Surya Ghar, KCC, etc. was undertaken. The progress of opening of brick & mortar branches of banks and deployment of BCs in unbanked villages was also reviewed.

Secretary, DFS, Sh. Sanjay Lohiya said that while significant progress has been made in deepening financial inclusion in the country through various flagship schemes of the Government, banks should make efforts for further enhancing their digital outreach and focus on end-to end digital processing of loans. Providing working capital loans through channels like credit lines on UPI and credit cards for micro-enterprises (CCME) was also explained. He discussed in detail the progress made by banks under Financial Inclusion. He urged the Private Sector Banks to increase their participation in financial inclusion schemes.

During the meeting, Secretary DFS, Sh. Sanjay Lohiya directed the banks to increase awareness of claim eligibility in Jansuraksha insurance schemes so that the nominees receive the amount after the unfortunate demise of the beneficiary. Banks were also advised to take specific care while handling grievances related to claims under these schemes. He also asked banks to enrol all new beneficiaries of PMJJBY & PMSBY through the Jan Suraksha portal as the portal will be integrated with all banks and insurers thereby enhancing the quality of data and ease of operations. During the meeting, ways to increase the persistency ratio of the Atal pension yojana were also discussed.

Sh. Lohiya urged banks to participate whole heartedly in the forth- coming FI saturation campaign from 21.10.2026 to 31.12.2026 and give more thrust on serving the marginalized sections of the society and fulfilling their banking needs.

2319694.title: CAQM mandates Installation of PTZ Cameras at Industries to ensure Comprehensive Real-time Monitoring of Fuel Use and Compliance in NCR
2319694.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2319694.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
CAQM mandates Installation of PTZ Cameras at Industries to ensure Comprehensive Real-time Monitoring of Fuel Use and Compliance in NCR
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 5:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has issued an order mandating expansion of Pan-Tilt-Zoom (PTZ) cameras at industries in the National Capital Region (NCR) to ensure comprehensive real-time monitoring of fuel consumption and compliance with its directions. The measure is aimed at strengthening vigilance, monitoring and compliance by industries, particularly in view of the adverse impact of industrial emissions on air quality in the NCR and adjoining areas, which assumes greater significance during the winter months.

In view of the persistent use of unapproved fuels, the Commission has expanded the areas to be captured by PTZ cameras at industrial units to make the coverage comprehensive and for effective monitoring and compliance. Apart from the locations of PTZ cameras already prescribed by CPCB, the Commission has directed that industries shall now also install additional PTZ cameras by 31.10.2026, as per the following Standard Operating Procedure (SOP):

  1. Location of Cameras

  • Cameras will be installed to capture all fuel storage areas.

  • Cameras will be installed to capture all fuel charging points.

  • In case of use of gas-based fuel, the gauge/ meter of the gas is to be captured by the camera.

 

  1. Real Time Streaming

  • Real-time streaming of video feeds shall be made available to the servers of CPCB and respective SPCBs/ DPCC.

 

  1. Power Source

  • All industries shall ensure that these cameras and the connectivity have adequate power backup.

 

The Order also mandates CPCB and the concerned SPCBs/ DPCC to develop portals and other necessary infrastructure to capture the real-time streaming of video feeds. This will facilitate remote monitoring of fuel-use practices by industries and help in ensuring the compliance of Commission’s Statutory Directions. The status of implementation of the said measures shall be submitted to the Commission by the concerned SPCBs/ DPCC by 01.11.2026.

In the light of pollution caused by industrial emissions, the Commission had also prescribed a standard list of approved fuels for NCR for various applications, including industrial use. However, the Flying Squads of the Commission, during incognito inspections of industries across the NCR, have reported use of unapproved fuels in multiple instances. In view of the persistent use of unapproved fuels, the Commission has considered real-time monitoring of fuel consumption by industries necessary.

Considering the poor air quality in Delhi-NCR and with a view to ensure strict vigilance, monitoring and compliance through self-regulation, the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) had earlier directed installation of Pan-Tilt-Zoom (PTZ) cameras along with real-time Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS) by industries. The prescribed locations for installation of PTZ cameras include capturing the OCEMS port-hole as well as flue gas emissions from the stack in case of textile and food processing units having boilers and capturing fume extraction system areas and furnace feeding areas in metal units.

2319695.title: Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue 2027: 1,45,26,013 attempts in Nationwide Quiz; Shortlisted Youth Advance to Essay Round
2319695.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2319695.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue 2027: 1,45,26,013 attempts in Nationwide Quiz; Shortlisted Youth Advance to Essay Round
Shortlisted participants to submit 500-word essays on MY Bharat Portal till 15th October, 2026
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 5:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD) 2027, a flagship youth engagement initiative of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat), has successfully completed the Viksit Bharat Quiz. The Quiz drew an overwhelming response from young Indians across the country, with 1,45,26,013 attempts recorded during the selection process.

The VBYLD 2027 aims to provide young citizens with a structured, merit-based platform to share their ideas, perspectives and innovative solutions towards the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. The initiative aligns with the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to create opportunities for talented youth to participate in public life and contribute to nation-building.

A Merit-Based National Youth Leadership Journey

VBYLD 2027 follows a structured, multi-stage selection process designed to identify and nurture youth leadership from the grassroots to the national level. The Viksit Bharat Challenge follows the pathway:

Viksit Bharat Quiz → Viksit Bharat Essay Challenge → District PPT Championship → State/UT VBYLD → National VBYLD

The Viksit Bharat Quiz, the first stage of the VBYLD 2027 selection process, was conducted on the MY Bharat portal from 17 August to 30 September 2026, with a corresponding Quiz also hosted on the MyGov platform. The Quiz comprised 20 questions, with a maximum score of 20 marks and a time limit of 10 minutes.

About 5.7 lakh youth who qualified in the Quiz round will proceed to the next stage, the Viksit Bharat Essay Challenge, and submit a 500-word essay on the MY Bharat portal on the theme designated for the region. The themes for the essay and presentation rounds are as under. The detailed mapping of States with themes is available on MY Bharat Portal:

  1. Future Governance, Urban Transformation & Citizen Services
  2. Climate Security, Borders & Sustainable Mountain Development
  3. Demographic Dividend & Human Capital Development
  4. Sustainable Industrialization & Resource-led Growth
  5. Act East, Connectivity & Cultural Leadership
  6. Manufacturing, Entrepreneurship & Green Growth
  7. Tribal Leadership, Natural Resources & Inclusive Development
  8. Innovation Economy, Tourism & Creative Industries
  9. Technology, Innovation, Future Readiness
  10. Blue Economy, Human Capital & Global Competitiveness

 

Essays may be written in any of 23 languages on the MY Bharat portal till 15th October, 2026. The most promising young contributors will be shortlisted for an in-person presentation round at the district level, which will be conducted across all districts for the first time. Selected participants will then proceed to the State/UT VBYLD to present at that stage.  Participants selected from all States/UTs under 10 regional themes will form part of the National contingent of the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD).

 

******

Pawan Singh Faujdar

2319668.title: HAL Koraput Delivers 2,000th Aero-Engine, Marking Six Decades of Propulsion Manufacturing
2319668.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
HAL Koraput Delivers 2,000th Aero-Engine, Marking Six Decades of Propulsion Manufacturing
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh calls for strengthening indigenous design, development, testing and manufacturing of advanced aero-engines
AL-31FP production capacity to rise from 30 to 50 engines annually with Rs 335 crore investment
Second Shakti engine production line to be established with Rs 218 crore investment; capacity to reach up to 100 engines annually
Government pursuing indigenous high-thrust engine programme with investment of about Rs 5,000 crore
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 4:57PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh witnessed the delivery of the 2,000th aero-engine by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Koraput Division and announced the establishment of a second production line for Shakti engines on October 06, 2026. Describing the milestone as a significant achievement in India’s aerospace journey, he called for strengthening indigenous capabilities in the design, development, testing, manufacturing and maintenance of advanced aero-engines, stressing that mastery of propulsion technology is essential for self-reliance in the aerospace and defence sector.

Congratulating the engineers, technicians, scientists and skilled workforce of HAL Koraput, Shri Rajnath Singh said the delivery of 2,000 engines represents 2,000 significant contributions to the operational capability of the Defence Forces and reflects six decades of engineering expertise and technological experience since the Division was established in 1964.

The Raksha Mantri highlighted HAL Koraput’s contribution to military aviation, noting that its engines have powered frontline aircraft including the MiG-21, MiG-27, MiG-29 and Su-30MKI. He stated that while production provides new capability, overhaul extends service life, making both critical for military preparedness. He appreciated HAL Koraput’s indigenous repair and overhaul capability, with more than 9,000 engines overhauled so far, and noted that indigenisation of components and reduced turnaround time are contributing to operational readiness and extended service life of critical defence assets.

Describing the aero-engine as the ‘heart’ of an aircraft, Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised that reliable propulsion is essential to effectively utilise advanced airframes, radars, weapons and avionics. He highlighted the need for expertise in precision manufacturing, advanced materials, metallurgy, cooling technologies, testing and stringent quality assurance. He noted that aero-engine technology combines advanced superalloys, thermal-barrier coatings and sophisticated cooling systems for reliable performance under extreme conditions, making mastery of propulsion technology a mastery of some of the most advanced industrial capabilities.

Raksha Mantri underlined that aerospace self-reliance must extend to indigenous aero-engine capability, particularly for the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme. He highlighted the proposed investment of around Rs 5,000 crore, indigenisation of raw materials in partnership with Mishra Dhatu Nigam Limited (MIDHANI) and establishment of India’s first indigenous high-thrust engine testing facility. He stressed that a sovereign aerospace ecosystem requires indigenous capabilities across materials, design, manufacturing, testing and Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO).

Highlighting HAL’s performance in meeting Defence Forces’ requirements, Shri Rajnath Singh noted that the Government placed an order for 240 AL-31FP engines with HAL in 2024 for the Su-30MKI. Despite global supply-chain disruptions and raw-material challenges, HAL delivered the first engine ahead of schedule and has delivered 63 engines against a target of 60 by the end of the second year.

Raksha Mantri announced that HAL is enhancing annual AL-31FP production capacity from 30 to 50 engines with an investment of Rs 335 crore. He also announced a second Shakti engine production line with an investment of Rs 218 crore. The new line will manufacture up to 100 engines annually and is scheduled to be fully established by 2028-29, catering to indigenous helicopters including Dhruv Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH) and Prachand Light Combat Helicopter (LCH).

Emphasising the need for reliable indigenous propulsion for India’s helicopter ecosystem, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the Defence Forces require engines that are available when needed, supported throughout their lifecycle and upgraded with evolving technology. He noted that aero-engine development is a long-term endeavour requiring sustained investment, specialised testing, skilled manpower and a strong industrial ecosystem, with focus on repeatable, reliable and scalable production, design, critical materials and superalloys.

Raksha Mantri called for greater integration of MSMEs, start-ups, private industry, academia and research institutions into the propulsion ecosystem. He called upon HAL to develop Koraput not merely as an engine production facility but as a broader aerospace propulsion ecosystem by nurturing suppliers, mentoring MSMEs, supporting start-ups and young engineers, collaborating with universities and research institutions, and developing capabilities for critical components.

Highlighting Odisha’s growing importance in the defence and aerospace ecosystem, Shri Rajnath Singh noted the State’s strategic location, long coastline, ports, mineral resources, industrial infrastructure and skilled manpower. He stated that strategic infrastructure, including DRDO’s Integrated Test Range at Chandipur, along with recent initiatives of the Odisha Government, provides a strong foundation for growth of the aerospace and defence manufacturing ecosystem. 

Appreciating the initiatives of the Odisha Government, under Chief Minister Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Raksha Mantri highlighted the approval for an Aerospace and Defence Equipment Manufacturing Complex at Gajamara, Dhenkanal. He called upon HAL to develop Koraput as a nucleus of a broader aerospace propulsion ecosystem by developing suppliers, mentoring MSMEs, providing opportunities to young engineers and start-ups in advanced technology areas, collaborating with universities and research institutions, creating opportunities for skilled local youth, and developing indigenous manufacturing capabilities for critical engine components.

Urging the HAL Koraput team to raise standards in quality, productivity, indigenisation, innovation and delivery timelines, Shri Rajnath Singh described the 2,000th engine as a significant milestone and called for using it as a foundation to build an Indian aerospace industry capable of designing, developing, manufacturing and supporting advanced propulsion systems. He congratulated the HAL Koraput team, Indian Air Force, industry partners, MSMEs, scientists, engineers, technicians and the people of Odisha on the occasion.

Chief Minister of Odisha Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, Deputy Chief of the Air Staff Air Marshal Tejpal Singh, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD), HAL Shri Ravi K, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD), MIDHANI Dr. S.V.S. Narayana Murty and Joint Secretary (Aerospace Wing & DOMW) Ms Manisha Chandra were also present on the occasion.

2319660.title: National Postal Week 2026 to be Celebrated from 9th to 15th October, Commencing with World Post Day on 9th October
2319660.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
National Postal Week 2026 to be Celebrated from 9th to 15th October, Commencing with World Post Day on 9th October
‘World Post Day: One Postal Network, Infinite Possibilities’
Week-long Celebrations to Highlight India Post’s Enduring Role in Connecting Citizens and Building a Modern, Inclusive and Citizen-Centric Postal Network
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 4:49PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Posts (DoP) is celebrating National Postal Week, from 9th to 15th October, commencing with the World Post Day on 9th October.

The theme of this year’s World Post Day is ‘World Post Day: One Postal Network, Infinite Possibilities.’

The National Postal Week 2026 will focus on the Department’s continued efforts to make postal services more convenient, accessible and responsive to the evolving needs of citizens.

Through initiatives such as N-Gen Post Offices and Jan Sewa Connect Post Offices, the Department is creating modern and inclusive service spaces that are designed to respond to the changing expectations of citizens. At the same time, digital platforms such as the Dak Sewa App and Dak Mitra App are making postal services easier to access and use. These initiatives are contributing towards a more connected, responsive and technology-enabled India Post, equipped to meet the needs of the future.

The week-long celebrations will feature specially themed days, with each day highlighting an important dimension of the Department’s contribution towards building a modern, inclusive and citizen-centric postal ecosystem. The celebrations will showcase the role of India Post in strengthening financial inclusion, promoting digital empowerment, facilitating efficient mail and parcel services, encouraging philately and advancing technology and innovation across the postal network.

The celebrations will commence with World Post Day on 9th October 2026 (Friday). The day will highlight the universal significance of postal services and the enduring role of the postal network in connecting people, communities and businesses. It will also provide an opportunity to recognise the contribution of postal services towards strengthening communication and access to essential services.

Fun with Philately Day will be observed on 12th October 2026 (Monday), highlighting the rich cultural, educational and historical dimensions of philately. The day will encourage greater appreciation of stamps and postal heritage while promoting philately as an engaging means of learning and preserving the nation’s diverse heritage.

Financial Inclusion & CCS Day will be observed on 13th October 2026 (Tuesday). The day will highlight the contribution of the Department of Posts towards strengthening financial inclusion and extending access to financial services through its extensive postal network, particularly by reaching citizens across diverse geographical and socio-economic backgrounds.

Mails & Parcels Day will be observed on 14th October 2026 (Wednesday), focusing on the Department’s continued efforts to provide reliable, efficient and accessible mail and parcel services. The day will highlight the importance of India Post in connecting individuals, businesses and institutions across the country and facilitating the movement of communications and goods.

The celebrations will conclude with Technology & Innovation Day on 15th October 2026 (Thursday). The day will showcase the Department’s continuing adoption of technology and innovative solutions to improve postal operations, enhance service delivery and provide citizens with greater convenience and accessibility.

National Postal Week 2026 will provide an opportunity to celebrate the rich legacy of India Post while highlighting its transformation in response to the changing needs of citizens. The celebrations will reinforce the vision of India Post as a modern, inclusive, technology-enabled and citizen-centric postal network, continuing to connect people and communities while creating new possibilities through innovation, accessibility and service excellence.

The celebrations reaffirm the enduring role of the Department of Posts in delivering essential services while highlighting its continuous journey of modernisation, innovation and citizen-centric service delivery.

The Department of Posts (DoP), with its vast network, trust and reliability, continues to serve as a vital link connecting people, communities and businesses across the nation.

2319609.title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Addresses Second Convocation of Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University
2319609.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Addresses Second Convocation of Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University
“Sanskrit is the Golden String that Connects India’s Many Languages into One Grand Garland”: Vice-President
“Our Ancient Knowledge Must Be Preserved, Studied, Interpreted and Made Available to Future Generations”: Vice-President
“A Favourable Ecosystem Has Been Created for the Resurgence of Sanskrit Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Leadership”: Vice-President
“Use Social Media Wisely; Do Not Let the Virtual World Take You Away from the Real World”: Vice-President
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 4:25PM by PIB Delhi

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed the Second Convocation of Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University at Qutub Institutional Area, New Delhi. He congratulated the graduating students, their parents, faculty members and the University community on the occasion. He also led the gathering in taking the “No to Drugs” pledge and presented gold medals to meritorious graduating students.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Second Convocation of Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University in New Delhi. He highlighted Sanskrit as the “golden string” connecting India’s many languages and emphasised the need to preserve, study and take India’s ancient knowledge traditions to future generations.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) October 6, 2026

Highlighting the University’s journey from a Sanskrit Vidyapeetha to a Central University, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that it was now time for the institution to establish itself as a leading international centre of excellence for Sanskrit studies, fulfilling the vision of its founder, former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri. Paying tribute to Shri Shastri, he said that his immortal call of “Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan” was not merely a slogan but reflected India’s resolve to protect its borders and ensure food security.

The Vice-President lauded the University for securing the highest NAAC grade of A++ and for conducting research across diverse domains of the Indian Knowledge Tradition. He said that while every Indian language has enriched the nation, Sanskrit is the “golden string” connecting the pearls of India’s many languages into one grand garland. He also appreciated the University’s efforts to keep Sanskrit alive across the campus through Subhashitas, its 44-year tradition of publishing the Vidyapeeth Panchang, and its teaching of classical disciplines including Prakrit and Vastu Shastra.

Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan emphasised that India’s development must remain rooted in its civilisational heritage. He said that several initiatives under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi have created a favourable ecosystem for the resurgence of Sanskrit and promotion of the Indian Knowledge System. Referring to the National Education Policy 2020 and the Ashtadashi scheme, he said that rare Sanskrit texts must not be allowed to disappear and should be preserved, studied and made accessible to future generations.

Calling for greater scholarly engagement with India’s manuscript heritage, the Vice-President urged the University’s teachers and students to undertake the discovery, preservation, critical editing and publication of unpublished Sanskrit manuscripts. Referring to the Gyan Bharatam Mission, he said that the initiative, with a foundational corpus of ₹500 crore for manuscript preservation and documentation, is bringing India’s vast manuscript heritage to the people of India and the world.

Addressing the graduating students, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan urged them to remain lifelong learners and to carry forward the values imparted by their Acharyas and parents. In the age of Artificial Intelligence, he called upon them to harness technology for the preservation and promotion of Sanskrit.

The Vice-President urged the youth to stay away from drugs and substance abuse, and to choose discipline, sports, good company and meaningful pursuits. He also advised students to use social media wisely and in moderation, investing their time in reading, learning, skill development and building genuine relationships.

During the ceremony, the Vice-President also released three publications: ‘Amnaya Kalpataru’, ‘Vidyamitram’ and ‘Shodha Prabha’ (July–September 2026).

The ceremony was attended by Shri Sukanta Majumdar, Union Minister of State for Education and DoNER; Prof. Murli Manohar Pathak, Vice-Chancellor of Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University; distinguished scholars, Acharyas, officers, faculty members, staff, students, parents and Sanskrit enthusiasts.

Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India calls for equal attention to Adaptation, Mitigation and Means of Implementation at Pre-COP31
There can’t be a ‘One-Size-Fits-All’ approach; Equity and CBDR-RC must for Meaningful and Sustained Climate Action: Shri Bhupender Yadav 
India offers to share its Coastal Resilience and Space-based Expertise with Pacific Partners
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 4:22PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav is leading the Indian Delegation at the UNFCCC’s Pre-COP31 meetings being co-hosted by Australia, Fiji and Tuvalu. 

Addressing the Leaders’ Plenary at Fiji, the Union Minister today called for equal attention to adaptation, mitigation and means of implementation as the world moves towards COP31. He emphasized that the principles of Equity and Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC) must be upheld in letter and spirit for meaningful and sustained climate action across countries.

Shri Yadav stressed that there cannot be a “one-size-fits-all” pathway to climate action. He highlighted that local studies and assessments are important for finding solutions to emerging challenges of the area. These solutions, in turn,  indicate the mitigation and adaptation measures required and the commensurate resources required for the same, he added.

The Union Minister said India, with its vast coastline and islands, fully understands the challenges faced by Pacific Island Countries. He informed that India has developed a broad knowledge base and expertise in the area of ocean science through our premier institutions and bodies like Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management (NCSCM), National Centre for Coastal Research (NCCR). 

Shri Yadav highlighted that India has developed knowledge and expertise in vulnerability assessment of coasts, mapping of shoreline changes, development of marine spatial plans, integrated management plans for coastal areas and unlocking the potential of the Blue Economy. Further, he stated, India is also using its space ecosystem, Earth-observation capabilities and space-based applications for shoreline monitoring, inundation assessment, cyclone and extreme-weather early warning, and climate-risk assessment. He offered to share this knowledge and expertise with its Pacific partners.

The Minister said India has always stood firmly with its Pacific partners and is working closely with them in areas including health and wellness, renewable energy, resilient infrastructure, early warning, IT, agriculture and capacity building. Referring to his visit to Tuvalu, Shri Yadav said the Tuvalu Coastal Adaptation Project was a strong reflection of how international cooperation, particularly the provision of means of implementation, can translate into tangible resilience on the ground. The Minister reiterated that the experience has reinforced the importance of finding local solutions to emerging climate challenges. 

Pre-COP is a preparatory meeting held a few weeks before the annual UN Climate Change Conference, which this year will be held in Antalya, Türkiye, in November.

2319589.title: DRDO Conducts Maiden Live Jump of Advanced High-Altitude Parachute
2319589.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
DRDO Conducts Maiden Live Jump of Advanced High-Altitude Parachute
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 4:11PM by PIB Delhi

Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) conducted the maiden live jump of the Advanced High-Altitude Parachute (AHAP) at one of the highest-altitude drop zones, Nyoma (Mudh DZ).

The jump was executed at 16,000 feet above mean sea level (AMSL). The parachute was deployed at 15500 feet AMSL and landing was undertaken at Nyoma (Mudh DZ) which is at 13,700 feet. The jump proved the efficacy and tactical employability of the AHAP parachute at extremely High-Altitude Terrains.

Designed and developed by Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment (ADRDE), Agra, AHAP is a static line parachute system for mass drop of paratroopers.

The system has been manufactured by Ordnance Parachute Factory (OPF) Kanpur, inspected by DGAQA and certified by CEMILAC, RCMA Kanpur.

AHAP offers various deployment modes, has a very wide operational altitude range (up to 18000 ft) and has the safest rate of descent especially suited for the tactical requirements of the Indian Defence Forces for high-altitude terrains. Static line parachute jumps at these high altitudes are complex and inherently risky owing to very high opening shock and rate of descent.

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh complimented DRDO, Defence Forces, DPSUs and Industry on the successful maiden live jump of AHAP indigenous parachute system and termed it as another big step towards Aatmanirbhar Bharat.

Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D & Chairman, DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh congratulated the team members associated with the design and development of the system.

2319567.title: “Yuva Shakti is the Strength of Viksit Bharat”: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya
2319567.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2319567.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
“Yuva Shakti is the Strength of Viksit Bharat”: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya
MY Bharat’s Points, Rewards and Recognition Mechanism to Turn Youth Participation into Recognition, Opportunity and Leadership
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 3:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat), is operationalising a Points, Rewards and Recognition (PRR) Mechanism on the MY Bharat Portal to recognise and encourage sustained participation of young people in volunteering, experiential learning, youth development initiatives and other nation-building activities.

Highlighting the importance of youth participation in the nation-building process, Union Minister for Youth Affairs & Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya said, “Yuva Shakti is the strength of Viksit Bharat. Through MY Bharat’s PRR mechanism, the Modi Government is turning youth participation into recognition, opportunity and leadership.”

The PRR mechanism introduces a structured, milestone-based system through which youth will receive recognition, rewards and opportunities based on the points accumulated through their engagement on the MY Bharat Portal. The initiative seeks to motivate young people to sustain their participation in volunteering, experiential learning, civic engagement and youth development activities, while encouraging them to strive towards higher milestones.

Under the mechanism, youth achieving 1,000 points will receive a formal MY Bharat Letter of Recognition, signed by the Director, MY Bharat Division. At the 2,500-point milestone, eligible participants will be recognised through the official MY Bharat social media handles, subject to a consent-based mechanism for publication of their name, photograph and MY Bharat ID.

Youth attaining 5,000 points will be featured in a dedicated MY Bharat Digital Hall of Fame on the MY Bharat Portal. The Hall of Fame will showcase the achiever’s name, MY Bharat ID, photograph and a brief profile drawn from the public profile. A facility for other users to send messages to achievers may also be explored, subject to appropriate safeguards.

The mechanism provides progressively enhanced rewards at higher milestones. Youth achieving 7,500 points will receive the hardbound book Modi@20. Those reaching 10,000 points will be eligible to receive a signed hardbound copy of The Golden Road: How Ancient India Transformed the World by William Dalrymple, signed by the Hon’ble Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports. At the 20,000-point milestone, eligible achievers will receive a signed hardbound copy of Treasures of India: From Antiquity to Modernity by DK, signed by the Hon’ble Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports.

The higher milestones under the PRR mechanism are designed to provide young achievers with opportunities for direct interaction with senior leadership. At the 50,000-point milestone, eligible youth will have an opportunity to meet the Hon’ble Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports during an upcoming edition of the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD) or another suitable major youth engagement event. The eligible achievers will be identified from the Portal and their details verified by MY Bharat Headquarters.

At the highest proposed milestone of 1,00,000 points, eligible youth will have an opportunity to meet the Hon’ble Union Minister of Youth Affairs & Sports during an upcoming edition of VBYLD. The selected youth will be identified through the MY Bharat Portal and their details verified by MY Bharat Headquarters. The felicitation of youth achieving the 50,000 and 1,00,000-point milestones is proposed to commence from October 2027.

The PRR mechanism establishes a progressive pathway that begins with formal recognition and digital visibility and extends to tangible rewards and opportunities to engage with national youth leadership platforms. Through the initiative, MY Bharat seeks to create a sustained culture of participation, service and leadership among India’s youth.

The initiative reinforces the vision of “Samarth Yuva, Viksit Bharat”, recognising that active and empowered youth are central to India’s journey towards a developed nation. By acknowledging individual contributions and creating opportunities for further engagement, the PRR mechanism seeks to inspire young citizens to continue their journey of leadership, community service and nation-building through MY Bharat.

2319565.title: Cabinet passes  resolution congratulating Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 25 Years of Unbroken Leadership
2319565.body_html:
Cabinet
Cabinet passes resolution congratulating Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 25 Years of Unbroken Leadership
10 Defining Highlights of the Union Cabinet Resolution
Posted On: 06 OCT 2026 3:50PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet today passed a resolution congratulating Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on completing 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government. Far more than a customary tribute, it celebrates the extraordinary journey of PM Modi guided by principle of Nation First and Citizen First. Three overwhelming mandates in Gujarat and support in three successive Lok Sabha elections reflect the enduring trust that public have reposed in PM Narendra Modi

These ten salient features capture the unbroken thread connecting his leadership of Gujarat with his leadership of India.

  1. From Gujarat to India A Development Vision Grows

The resolution traces how PM Modi carried Gujarat’s successful initiatives to the national stage. SWAGAT, through which he personally heard citizens’ grievances, received the United Nations Public Service Award in 2010. It later inspired PRAGATI, bringing governments together to review stalled projects, resolve obstacles and accelerate completion. Jyotigram’s separate agricultural electricity feeders similarly became a national approach, extending Gujarat’s experience across India.

  1. Compassion for the Poor Becomes Dignity at Scale

PM Modi’s sensitivity towards poverty grew from watching his mother struggle with everyday hardships and encountering deprivation during his travels. The resolution connects these experiences with programmes delivering homes, water, banking and healthcare. Nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty show how personal understanding became public action, bringing families dignity.

  1. Empowerment Opens Doors Across Society

PM Modi’s determination to help people shape their futures runs through the resolution. Approximately 3.5 crore women became LakhpatiDidis, while the Nari Shakti VandanAdhiniyam provided for women’s reservation. Startups, skills and education reform expanded youth opportunities. PM-KISAN transfers exceeded ₹4 lakh crore, while PM-JANMAN brought focused support to particularly vulnerable tribal communities, extending development to those historically left behind.

  1. An Unwavering Commitment to Reform

The resolution gives particular emphasis to PM Modi’s willingness to pursue reform despite political risks. GST, welfare delivery reforms and the replacement of colonial laws demonstrate his determination to address longstanding challenges. His appeals on cleanliness, digital payments and local products drew citizens into change. Reform emerges as a sustained commitment of his leadership, strengthened by conviction, public participation and national purpose.

  1. Building the Foundations of a Self-Reliant India

Under PM Modi’s leadership, Public capital expenditure rose from ₹2 lakh crore to over ₹12 lakh crore, alongside highway expansion and railway electrification. Electronics production increased from around ₹2 lakh crore to more than ₹13 lakh crore. Defence production and semiconductor manufacturing further reflect his determination to strengthen India’s ability to meet its needs.

  1. Technology Serves Citizens and Expands National Ambition

PM Modi’s faith in technology emerges through achievements spanning everyday services and scientific frontiers. Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and mobile connectivity improved welfare delivery, while UPI transformed payments. Developing India’s own COVID vaccines and landing Chandrayaan-3 near the Moon’s south pole demonstrated PM Modi’s vision of a scientifically capable, self-reliant, Atmanirbhar Bharat. Private space participation and work in artificial intelligence, quantum technology and biotechnology carry forward the vision celebrated in the resolution: technology improving lives while expanding national possibilities.

7. Steadfast Leadership Through Turbulent Times

The resolution highlights PM Modi’s ability to give India direction through global upheaval. During COVID, he united the country, backed domestic vaccine development and enabled rapid vaccination. During the West Asia crisis, timely decisions and energy security measures helped India withstand disruption. His leadership combined immediate responses with capabilities built over years, giving the country resilience and confidence in difficult times.

8. Decisive Leadership Secures Peace and Confidence

2016 Surgical strikes, 2019 Balakot Air Strikes and 2025 Operation Sindoor illustrate the national security red lines established under PM Modi. The resolution places these alongside the removal of Article 370, One Rank One Pension and creation of the Chief of Defence Staff’s post. Action against Maoist terrorism and peace efforts in the Northeast bring out leadership combining national resolve with development, stability and public trust.

9. India’s Voice Grows Stronger on the World Stage

The resolution links India’s rising stature with PM Modi’s ability to build cooperation across divisions. Consensus at G20 and BRICS, advocacy for the Global South and the African Union’s G20 inclusion reflect his diplomatic leadership. Vaccine Maitri demonstrated how India’s capabilities could serve others. Honours from 36 countries underline the international regard accompanying PM Modi and India’s growing influence and contribution to shared solutions.

10. Progress Draws Strength from Heritage and Responsibility

PM Modi’s vision unites development, cultural confidence and environmental responsibility. Climate action progressed from Gujarat’s dedicated department to renewable energy expansion and international partnerships. Yoga, millets, Kashi Vishwanath Dham and Ram Lalla’s consecration strengthened India’s connection with its heritage. The resolution culminates in renewed commitment to his vision of collective effort towards a prosperous, self-reliant and developed India by 2047.
