2318052.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Government Extends Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products ( RoDTEP) Scheme upto 31st December 2026
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 11:00AM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Commerce, has vide Notification No. 41/2026-27 dated 30th September 2026 extended the continuation of Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) Scheme upto 31st December 2026  and shall be available for exports made by Domestic Tariff Area  (DTAs) Units, Advance Authorisation (AA) Holders, Special Economic Zone (SEZ) Units and Export Oriented Units(EOUs).

The RoDTEP Scheme refunds embedded, un-rebated Central, State and local duties, taxes and levies borne on exported products — including prior-stage cumulative indirect taxes

The existing RoDTEP rates and value caps, as notified in Appendix 4R and Appendix 4RE as applicable on 30th September 2026 shall continue unchanged during the aforesaid period.

The above measure reflects the Government's commitment to provide support to the exporters by creating a level playing field in international markets vis-à-vis competing economies.

2318047.title: Ministry of Steel undertakes Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters 6
2318047.body_html:
Ministry of Steel
Ministry of Steel undertakes Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters 6
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 10:19AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Steel and its Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) are actively participating in the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 6, being conducted from 2nd October to 31st October 2026.

The Preparatory Phase of the campaign, from 15th September to 30th September 2026, has been completed. During this phase, the Ministry and its CPSEs completed the necessary preparations and set targets for the Implementation Phase.

During the Implementation Phase from 2nd October to 31st October 2026, the Ministry and its CPSEs will focus on the following activities:

  • Cleanliness Campaign: 301 cleanliness activities will be undertaken at various offices and locations.
  • Disposal of Files: Efforts will be made to dispose of 20,763 physical files and 9,056 e-files.
  • Public Grievances: Special focus will be given to the disposal of 37 pending public grievances, with the aim of bringing the pendency down to zero.

The campaign will focus on timely disposal of pending matters, including references from MPs, PMO, VIPs, Cabinet and State Governments. It will also focus on cleanliness, disposal of old files, proper record management and better use of office space.

Through SCDPM 6, the Ministry of Steel and its CPSEs will work towards reducing pendency, faster disposal of matters, better service delivery and maintaining a clean and efficient working environment.

Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Ministry of Law and Justice
Union Minister of State (I/C) for Law and Justice Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal Leads Tree Plantation Drive at IIAC.
Posted On: 02 OCT 2026 7:38AM by PIB Delhi

As part of the Special Campaign 6 and Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026, the Department of Legal Affairs, Ministry of Law and Justice, organised a Tree Plantation Drive on 01.10.2026 at the India International Arbitration Centre (IIAC), Vasant Kunj, New Delhi under the theme of "Ek ped Maa ke naam" on the eve of Gandhi Jayanti.

The Plantation drive was led by Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Hon’ble Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice. Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs and Chairperson  IIAC, along with senior officers / officials of the Department and IIAC participated in the event. The  Hon’ble Minister, Law Secretary &  Chairperson  IIAC, Senior officers of the Department  and IIAC planted  saplings on the IIAC campus.

“True cleanliness begins in the mind (Mann ki Swachhta),” says the Minister, recalling Mahatma Gandhi’s Champaran experience

Addressing the gathering, the Hon’ble Minister said that cleanliness is not limited to keeping streets and public spaces clean; it must begin with a clean mind, pure thoughts and a sense of duty towards society.

He said that Swachhata Hi Seva is a people’s movement in which every individual has a role to play. He noted that 2 October, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, reminds the nation that cleanliness, discipline and service were integral to Bapu’s vision of a free and self-reliant India.

Recalling Mahatma Gandhi’s stay in Champaran in 1917, the Hon’ble Minister highlighted how Gandhiji initiated efforts towards sanitation and hygiene, which became part of a wider mass movement and contributed to addressing the grievances of indigo farmers.

The Minister said that the lesson from Champaran remains relevant today: Swachhata is a mission of empathy and shared responsibility, and not merely a campaign.

Shri Meghwal expressed confidence that, through the collective efforts of all stakeholders, IIAC would develop into a global, efficient and credible centre for arbitration. He said that the Centre should reflect the same values of transparency, discipline and service that Swachhata Hi Seva represents.

Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs and Chairperson, IIAC, said that cleanliness has two dimensions — the cleanliness of our surroundings and the cleanliness of the mind — and one remains incomplete without the other. He appreciated the efforts of IIAC and stressed that institutions have a responsibility to adopt sustainable practices and contribute meaningfully to the objectives of the Swachh Bharat Mission. He assured that IIAC is committed to establishing itself as a global, efficient and credible institution, contributing to India’s emergence as a preferred seat for international arbitration.

Shri Navin Kumar Singh, CEO, IIAC, thanked the Hon’ble Minister, Secretary and other dignitaries for their participation in the programme. He reaffirmed IIAC’s commitment to environmental responsibility and sustainable practices.

The programme concluded with a pledge to sustain cleanliness initiatives and promote a greener and more sustainable environment.

2317998.title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code has strengthened credit discipline, improved recovery climate and contributed to ease of doing business: Harsh Malhotra, MoS, Corporate Affairs Ministry
2317998.body_html:
Ministry of Corporate Affairs
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code has strengthened credit discipline, improved recovery climate and contributed to ease of doing business: Harsh Malhotra, MoS, Corporate Affairs Ministry
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) celebrates its Tenth Annual Day
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 10:06PM by PIB Delhi

Minister of State for Corporate Affairs Ministry and Road Transport and Highways, Shri Harsh Malhotra inaugurated the 10th Annual Day celebrations of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi today, marking ten years of IBBI since its establishment on 1st October, 2016.

Chief guest Shri Harsh Malhotra in his inaugural address, observed that the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) has strengthened credit discipline, improved the recovery climate and contributed to the ease of doing business in the country. He noted the Government’s commitment to keep the Code responsive to emerging needs, including through the recent legislative amendments, and urged all stakeholders to work towards faster and value-maximising resolutions in the decade ahead.

MoS Shri Malhotra highlighted the need for improved adoption of emerging technologies, including AI, in IBC ecosystem. He noted that the efforts should be made towards faster resolutions and value maximisation as way forward.

Justice Shri Anupinder Singh Grewal, Hon’ble President, National Company Law Tribunal, reflected to the role of the Adjudicating Authority in the IBC framework. He highlighted the steps being taken to reduce delays in disposal of cases and recent improvements in speedier disposal of resolution plans. He noted various areas of reforms that may be considered in coming times including revision in admission thresholds, use of mediation, sector specific carveouts, etc.

Shri Indevar Pandey, Hon’ble Member, National Company Law Appellate Tribunal shared his perspective on the evolution of insolvency jurisprudence over the decade and the issues that may be considered in coming times. He highlighted that the IBC has seen seven sets of amendments to the Code in the last ten years. While noting the constraints involved in amending laws, he appreciated that amendments to the Code and regulations are being carried out in line with emerging needs in a timely manner. While noting the positive outcomes of IBC, he emphasised the need for timelines to be respected by all stakeholders.

Shri Ansuman Pattnaik, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, while noting the achievements of the IBC, highlighted the policy reforms undertaken to strengthen the Code, including the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Act, 2026. He noted key aspects of the amendment act and outlined the areas for the next phase of reforms in IBC framework and ecosystem.

Welcoming the guests, Shri Jayanti Prasad, Chairperson, IBBI, reflected on the ten-year journey of the Code and the Board. He noted that IBC has enabled substantial recoveries for creditors, rescued viable businesses across sectors, and brought about a lasting change in

debtor–creditor behaviour. He observed that the ecosystem now comprises over 4,400 Insolvency Professionals and over 6,000 Registered Valuers, highlighting the responsive, participative and evidence-based approach to regulation-making being adopted by IBBI.

As part of the Tenth Annual Day celebrations, an annual publication, “Shaping the Next Decade of IBC: The Road Ahead”, was released during the event. On this occasion, winners of the 7th National Online Quiz on the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, were also felicitated.

The event was also graced by imminent dignitaries like Justice Shri Anupinder Singh Grewal, Hon’ble President, National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Shri Indevar Pandey, Hon’ble Member, National Company Law Appellate Tribunal; and Shri Ansuman Pattnaik, Additional  Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs also honoured the occasion with their gracious presence. The event was also attended by Shri Jayanti Prasad, Chairperson, IBBI; Shri Sandip Garg, whole Time Member, IBBI; and Shri Bhushan Kumar Sinha, whole Time Member, IBBI. The event witnessed participation of eminent dignitaries and key stakeholders of the insolvency ecosystem.

2317994.title: District Opium Office, Mandsaur Second Division, Mandsaur, conducts awareness programme under Mission Yuva Raksha
2317994.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
District Opium Office, Mandsaur Second Division, Mandsaur, conducts awareness programme under Mission Yuva Raksha
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 9:43PM by PIB Delhi

The District Opium Office, Mandsaur Second Division, Mandsaur, organised an awareness programme under “Mission Yuva Raksha” at Sharda Public School, Pipliya Mandi, with the objective of sensitizing students about the harmful effects of drug abuse and creating awareness regarding the importance of a drug-free life.

At the beginning of the programme, the participants were provided with information about the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), its role, functions and contribution towards prevention of drug abuse and enforcement of narcotics-related laws.

Thereafter, a Question-and-Answer Competition was organized to make the awareness activities more effective, interactive and participatory. Through the competition, students were sensitized about the manner in which drug abuse can adversely affect an individual’s physical and mental health, family life, education, career and overall future. Important information was also shared regarding the harmful effects of various addictive substances, preventive measures and the role of youth in building a drug-free society.

At the conclusion of the programme, the participating students and other participants took a Drug-Free India Pledge, committing themselves to staying away from drugs and contributing actively towards the creation of a healthy and drug-free society.

The programme was successfully conducted with the coordination and cooperation of the Principal of Sharda Public School, Pipliya Mandi. Approx 150 students participated enthusiastically in the programme, and the participants gave highly positive and encouraging feedback regarding the awareness activities.

The programme aimed to create awareness among young people about the dangers of drug abuse and to motivate them to contribute towards building a drug-free, healthy and responsible society. The programme concluded successfully with active participation and positive engagement from the students.

2317976.title: Cooperation between the Nalanda University and the CSIR-Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (CSIR-TKDL) Unit for research and capacity-building in the areas of Traditional Knowledge (TK), Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), People’s Rights and Cultural Heritage
2317976.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Cooperation between the Nalanda University and the CSIR-Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (CSIR-TKDL) Unit for research and capacity-building in the areas of Traditional Knowledge (TK), Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), People’s Rights and Cultural Heritage
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 9:26PM by PIB Delhi

Nālandā University (NU) and the CSIR–Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (CSIR-TKDL) Unit have signed a Memorandum of Understanding today to establish a structured collaboration for academic, research and capacity-building cooperation in the areas of Traditional Knowledge (TK), Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), People’s Rights and Cultural Heritage, including Traditional Cultural Expressions (TCEs). The MoU was signed by Prof. Sachin Chaturvedi, Vice Chancellor, Nālandā University and Dr. Viswajanani J Sattigeri, Scientist-H and Head, CSIR-TKDL Unit, in the presence of the faculty members of the Nālandā University and senior officials of the CSIR-TKDL Unit.

 

Through the collaboration, the two organizations, Nālandā University and CSIR-TKDL Unit shall draw together their individual strengths to address their common interests on matters of TK, IPR, cultural heritage including the TCEs of Bihar. The cooperation shall focus on academic and research activities and intellectual exchanges, trainings, student internship and exchange visits and networking, among others.

Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Chaturvedi, Vice-Chancellor, Nālandā University, appreciated the significant efforts of the CSIR on the TKDL and its role in preventing the misappropriation India’s TK. He further noted that this collaboration would strengthen efforts to identify, document and disseminate TK and TCEs while creating greater awareness about IPRs and also training the younger generation on the matter. He highlighted the importance of systematically documenting, preserving, and making TK across subject areas such as ecological knoweldge of the communities, folklore, music, and others. He also opined that the TK may be made accessible in a manner that safeguards the interests of knowledge holders and communities, as well as the organizations’ commitment to evidence based R&D in Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS). He observed that the collaboration with TKDL would provide an important platform for integrating TK with contemporary academic research, documentation, IP awareness and interdisciplinary scholarship.

Dr. Sattigeri, Head, CSIR-TKDL Unit stated that India has been leading globally on all matters of TK, be it policies or initiatives such as the TKDL. She stated that the ancient Nālandā University speaks of the importance of collaboration between organizations, both nationally and internationally. This collaboration between CSIR-TKDL Unit with the new Nālandā University is envisaged to rejuvenate the past glory of Nalanda as both educational and research hub, with specific focus on the cultural heritage of India, and particularly, Bihar. 

The Parties are confident that the collaboration between Nālandā University and CSIR-TKDL Unit will contribute to the attainment of the objectives of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and National IPR Policy 2016 on TK, IPR and cultural heritage.

About Nālandā University:

Nālandā University has been established as an International University of “National Importance” under the aegis of the Ministry of External Affairs, Govt of India, at Rajgir, District-Nalanda, Bihar. The objectives of Nālandā University, deriving on its ancient heritage value and strong international cooperation,  are focused on the pursuit of intellectual, philosophical, historical and spiritual studies and others. The revival of Nālandā University aims at improving regional understanding and the appreciation of one another’s heritage and history, to build a community of learning where students, scholars, researchers and academicians can work together symbolizing the spirituality that unites all mankind.

About TKDL:

The TKDL database, first of its kind worldwide, was established in 2001 by the Government of India, through a collaboration between CSIR and Ministry of AYUSH. The key objective of the TKDL is to prevent the erroneous grant of patents on Indian traditional knowledge (TK) and deter misappropriation of the country’s heritage. Currently, the TKDL contains information on over 5.2 lakh formulations and practices of Indian Systems of Medicine such as Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, and Sowa Rigpa as well as Yoga from the traditional texts. The TK information from diverse languages and subject areas are transcribed into value-added information correlated with modern terminologies.

The TKDL information is presented in a digitized format in five international languages including English, German, French, Japanese and Spanish, therein breaking language and format barriers for ease of use by patent examiners. Currently, the TKDL database is available to 18 international patent offices through Non-Disclosure Agreements.

The TKDL is a global benchmark in the defensive protection of traditional knowledge and has been successful in protecting India’s interest against any possible misuse of its heritage. The impact has been significant, with over 375 patent applications world-over being revoked, rejected, amended, withdrawn or abandoned, based on the prior art evidences presented from the TKDL database.

2317962.title: CRIT and IIFT Organise Three-Day Orientation Course on Trade Negotiations
2317962.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
CRIT and IIFT Organise Three-Day Orientation Course on Trade Negotiations
Course Focused on Emerging Global Trade Issues, WTO Framework, Dispute Settlement and Specialised Areas of Trade Negotiations
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 8:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Centre for Research on International Trade (CRIT), New Delhi, in partnership with the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade (IIFT), New Delhi, organised a three-day Orientation Course on Trade Negotiations from 28 to 30 September 2026 in New Delhi. The programme provided participants with an overview of key concepts, institutions and contemporary issues relating to international trade and trade negotiations.

The academic programme on the first day covered sessions on “Emerging World Trade Scenario: Challenges & Opportunities and Introduction to Basic Concepts of Trade Theory”, “Introduction to WTO” and a panel discussion on WTO issues.

The second day featured sessions on “Labour/Environment/Sustainability and Trade”, “Legal Analysis & Treaty Interpretation of Trade Agreements”, “Trade Analysis/Trade Databases” and “Dispute Settlement”.

On the third day, participants joined specialised tracks. Track I covered “Trade Remedies”, “Rules of Origin” and “Non-Tariff Measures (NTMs)”, while Track II covered “Intellectual Property Rights (IPR)”, “Digital Trade” and “Services”.

The programme concluded with the Valedictory Session, which included the valedictory address by Professor & Head, CTIL, with additional charge as Professor & Head, CWS, Dr. James J. Nedumpara ; the keynote address by Vice Chancellor, IIFT Dr. K. Rangarajan; and the Special Address by Additional Secretary, Department of Commerce, Shri Amitabh Kumar. Professor, CWS & Head Admin, CRIT, Dr. Murali Kallummal, proposed the vote of thanks, followed by the distribution of certificates.

In his Special Address, Shri Amitabh Kumar highlighted the role of trade in supporting GDP growth, while noting the need for trade professionals to navigate an increasingly complex global trading environment, including neo-mercantilist approaches and measures such as the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR). Referring to India’s economic reforms since 1991 and its accession to the WTO in 1995, he highlighted the expanding scope of multilateral trade rules beyond goods to services, intellectual property rights and sustainability-related issues, and appreciated CRIT’s initiative in organising the capacity-building programme.

The three-day course provided participants with a structured understanding of the international trading system and trade negotiations, covering foundational concepts and the WTO framework, as well as the economic, legal and policy dimensions of contemporary trade. The specialised sessions further provided insights into key negotiating areas relevant to the evolving global trade landscape.

2317940.title: Union Minister Shri Hardeep Singh Puri commends energy sector resilience, insulation of domestic consumers from global price shocks, and massive upstream push under ‘Samudra Manthan’ and ‘GOBARdhan’
2317940.body_html:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
Union Minister Shri Hardeep Singh Puri commends energy sector resilience, insulation of domestic consumers from global price shocks, and massive upstream push under ‘Samudra Manthan’ and ‘GOBARdhan’
PNGRB Celebrates 20th Foundation Day; Launches National PNG Drive 3.0 and ‘MyPNG Portal’ to Accelerate India’s Transition to a Gas-Based Economy
National PNG Drive 3.0 and unified consumer digital portal ‘MyPNG Portal’ officially launched to enhance access and service delivery
PNGRB Excellence Awards 2026 presented to top-performing CGD and pipeline operators
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 8:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) celebrated its 20th Foundation Day today at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. The event was graced by the Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, alongside Dr. Neeraj Mittal, Secretary, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, senior government officials, and key industry leaders. Marking two decades of regulatory leadership, the milestone occasion focused on consumer empowerment, infrastructure expansion, digital transformation, safety assurance, and sustainable sectoral growth.

Major Initiatives & Key Launches

National PNG Drive 3.0: Building upon the success of PNG Drive 1.0 and 2.0, PNGRB launched National PNG Drive 3.0 to accelerate Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections across domestic and commercial sectors nationwide.

MyPNG Portal: A unified, national digital consumer portal was launched to streamline PNG services, improve access to information, and strengthen interactions between consumers and City Gas Distribution (CGD) entities.

PNGRB Excellence Awards 2026: Outstanding performers across CGD networks, Natural Gas Pipelines, and Petroleum Product Pipelines were recognized for operational excellence, safety standards, and infrastructure delivery.

India Steers Energy Resilience with Infrastructure Push and Upstream Investments

Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas highlighted India’s resilience in navigating global energy market volatility while advancing the nation’s transition towards a gas-based economy. He noted that despite global energy market volatility with international price spikes of 70%–80%, strategic central excise duty cuts on petrol and diesel helped keep domestic fuel prices stable and insulated Indian consumers.

To further strengthen energy security, the Minister highlighted major policy decisions, including allocations of ₹84,084 crore under the Samudra Manthan scheme and ₹23,731 crore for GOBARdhan. The opening of 1 million sq km of previously restricted sedimentary basins has helped in boosting domestic hydrocarbon exploration and gas availability.

The Minister also highlighted the rapid expansion of the gas distribution ecosystem. Nearly the entire country has now been authorized for City Gas Distribution, while approximately 35,000 km of natural gas pipelines have been authorized. The Unified Tariff framework has helped reduce regional disparities and improve access to gas in distant and underserved regions. LPG connection coverage has also expanded from 14.5 crore in 2014 to over 33 crore.

Reaffirming the nation’s commitment to increasing the share of natural gas in the primary energy basket from current level of around 6%, the Minister also pointed to the momentum generated by National PNG Drive 2.0. During the six-month drive from January to June 2026, around 12.10 lakh new PNG connections and 15.31 lakh DPNG registrations were achieved. The pace of daily DPNG additions increased from 4,702 to around 7,000, while daily additions of billed consumers rose from around 2,781 to around 7,500 during the same period.

During the West Asia crisis, the Government ensured continuity of essential gas supplies, while the CGD sector continued to expand PNG adoption and strengthen coordination with States and other stakeholders.

Addressing the gathering, the Secretary, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, emphasized the evolving role of regulation in driving actual gas adoption across sectors, stressing that success must now be measured not merely by pipeline length laid, but by actual gas consumption, molecule utilization, and the speed at which household PNG connections multiply. He encouraged CGD entities to leverage special schemes to reduce cost recovery timelines from 10–15 years to 2–3 years, thereby addressing major financial roadblocks to network expansion. He also underlined the importance of coordination between upstream, downstream, Oil PSUs and the Government to ensure an uninterrupted clean energy supply.

The Minister also highlighted PNGRB’s technology-enabled approach to regulation through the National Hydrocarbon Infrastructure Monitoring System (NHIMS), which brings together infrastructure, administrative, transport, geographical and satellite data on a common digital platform. The system is expected to strengthen monitoring, planning and regulatory oversight and enable more informed and timely decision-making.

Looking ahead, the Minister underscored the need for faster and more effective digital grievance redressal, timely expansion of CGD networks into new areas, healthy competition, stronger sectoral capacity and a regulatory framework that keeps pace with India’s sustainability and Net Zero objectives. PNGRB’s continued independence and arm’s-length position from administrative and commercial interests, together with a clear, transparent and predictable regulatory framework, will remain important in building confidence across the industry.

The Minister congratulated PNGRB on completing two decades and expressed his best wishes to its leadership, officers and the entire natural gas industry for continued progress in the years ahead.

2317937.title: Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas Shri Hardeep Singh Puri launches GOBARdhan Scheme to accelerate development of India’s Compressed Biogas sector
2317937.body_html:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas
Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas Shri Hardeep Singh Puri launches GOBARdhan Scheme to accelerate development of India’s Compressed Biogas sector
Integrated Central Sector Scheme brings assured offtake, stable pricing, capital assistance, pipeline connectivity, credit support and ecosystem development under a unified framework
GOBARdhan Handbook unveiled and Unified GOBARdhan Portal launched to support streamlined implementation of the Scheme
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 8:27PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri, today launched GOBARdhan, the Central Sector Scheme for development of the Compressed Biogas (CBG) sector.

The Scheme, approved by the Union Cabinet on 6 August 2026 with an outlay of ₹23,731 crore, provides a ten-year framework from FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36 for accelerating CBG development in India. The scheme aims to increase domestic CBG production nearly 10-fold (to around 5 MMSCMD) with a long-term framework that gives investors and lenders greater certainty.

The launch brought together stakeholders from across the CBG ecosystem, including representatives of Central Ministries, State Governments, CBG developers, oil and gas companies, City Gas Distribution entities, financial institutions, cooperatives, technology providers and other stakeholders.

The launch featured the unveiling of the GOBARdhan Handbook, a comprehensive reference guide to assist stakeholders, project developers, State Governments and financial institutions in understanding the Scheme and navigating its CBG interventions, alongside the Unified GOBARdhan Portal, a centralised digital platform designed to streamline applications, eliminate multi-channel processes and enhance transparency throughout processing and implementation.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Hardeep Singh Puri said that India’s growing energy requirements must be addressed through the combined objectives of availability, affordability and sustainability, with greater development of energy resources available within the country.

He said that CBG has particular relevance for India as it can convert crop residue, cattle dung and other organic resources into clean domestic energy, while generating organic manure and creating new economic opportunities in rural areas. Farmers, cooperatives, gaushalas and local enterprises can participate across feedstock collection, aggregation, transportation and processing, strengthening the circular link between agriculture and energy.

He called upon industry, financial institutions, States, cooperatives, technology providers and other stakeholders to translate the framework into operating plants and sustained CBG production, advancing India’s energy security, rural prosperity and the Prime Minister’s vision of Waste to Wealth and Annadata to Urjadata.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Neeraj Mittal, Secretary, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, highlighted that India currently meets nearly half of its natural gas requirement through imports and that CBG provides an opportunity to convert domestic organic waste into a domestic gas resource.

He said that the experience of the sector had also highlighted constraints relating to volatile revenues, fragmented support, limited long-term policy visibility, feedstock assurance, organic manure offtake and access to finance. GOBARdhan addresses these issues through the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas as the single nodal Ministry, predictable pricing, greater certainty of gas offtake, enhanced capital assistance, consolidated processes and greater use of digital monitoring.

The Secretary also highlighted the important role of State Governments in translating the national framework into projects on the ground, including through enabling State CBG policies, feedstock assessments, suitable land banks, faster approvals and infrastructure support.

An integrated framework for the CBG sector

A presentation on GOBARdhan outlined the Scheme architecture and the transition from multiple standalone interventions towards an integrated framework for the sector. GOBARdhan comprises six key interventions: CBG Offtake Assurance, CBG Pricing Framework, Capital Assistance for CBG Projects, Development of Pipeline Infrastructure, Credit Guarantee Support and the CBG Ecosystem Challenge Fund.

Under the offtake framework, CBG plants will be mapped to identified City Gas Distribution geographical areas or CBG clusters, enabling a dependable route to market. Under the CBG Obligation (CBO), the obligation to procure CBG rests with City Gas Distribution (CGD) entities. The procurement obligation has been prescribed at 3% in FY 2026–27, 4% in FY 2027–28 and 5% from FY 2028–29 onwards for the CNG (Transport) and PNG (Domestic) segment

The Scheme introduces an administered CBG price of ₹2,110 per MMBtu, providing greater revenue visibility to producers. Eligible greenfield projects can receive capital assistance of up to ₹2 crore per TPD of installed CBG capacity, including support for plant machinery, feedstock aggregation and FOM/LFOM processing and manure value-addition equipment.

To address gas evacuation constraints, support of up to 80% of eligible capital expenditure is available for pipelines connecting CBG clusters to trunk pipeline networks and up to 50% for standalone plants connecting to CGD networks.

A dedicated credit guarantee mechanism for eligible MSME-based CBG projects will cover up to 85% of the outstanding amount at default, subject to prescribed project limits. The guarantee cap is ₹20 crore per project for general MSME projects and ₹25 crore per project for women-led MSME projects, providing enhanced support to women entrepreneurs in the CBG sector.

The CBG Ecosystem Challenge Fund will support technology development, capacity building, feedstock assessment and aggregation, district-level ecosystem development and value addition in organic manure.

India’s CBG ecosystem has already established a foundation for further growth, with 217+ plants commissioned as of August 2026, with an installed capacity of more than 1,700 TPD. The Scheme aims to increase domestic CBG production nearly ten-fold over its ten-year implementation period.

The Scheme is expected to generate significant economic and environmental benefits, including more than ₹40,000 crore in foreign-exchange savings, over ₹75,000 crore added to GDP and more than 1.5 lakh jobs. It is also expected to replace 10 million tonnes of fossil fuel with clean gas, reduce more than 40 million tonnes of CO₂ emissions and support the production of 250 million tonnes of organic manure.

2317932.title: MY Bharat-NSS Organises Nationwide “Health Walk/Run” Under Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan
2317932.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2317932.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
MY Bharat-NSS Organises Nationwide “Health Walk/Run” Under Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan
Over 1.11 lakh youth participate in Health Walk/Run, Heritage Walk and Nasha Mukt Yuva Sankalp across 198 institutions
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 8:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, through MY Bharat-National Service Scheme (NSS), organised a nationwide “Health Walk/Run – Step Up, Stay Addiction-Free” today as part of the “Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat” campaign. The activity marked the Week 3 intervention under the campaign’s Month 1 theme, “My Health, My Pride,” and was conducted across 198 targeted institutions and their adopted villages, mobilising youth and communities around the message of healthy and addiction-free living.

The nationwide initiative aimed to promote regular physical activity and healthy lifestyle choices while creating a visible demonstration of young people’s commitment towards an addiction-free society. The events commenced with guided warm-up sessions led by physical training instructors and fitness club trainers, followed by flag-offs by local sports officials, youth leaders and other dignitaries. Participants then undertook designated walk/run routes, led by MY Bharat Youth Volunteers, along with community members and local stakeholders.

As part of the initiative, several locations also incorporated Heritage Walks, enabling participants to combine physical activity with an appreciation of local history and heritage. The walks provided an opportunity for youth to engage with their communities while promoting fitness, outdoor activities and a sense of pride in local heritage.

The events also featured the Nasha Mukt Yuva Sankalp, through which participating youth pledged to maintain a substance-free lifestyle and contribute towards creating awareness about the harmful effects of substance abuse. Volunteers used banners, placards and slogans along the routes and at event venues to reinforce the campaign message and shared information on available counselling and support services.

The nationwide drive witnessed 1,11,112 participants. The Health Walk/Run component recorded participation of 39,288 youth, comprising 19,012 male and 20,276 female participants, covering a cumulative distance of 712.3 kilometres. The Heritage Walk component witnessed participation of 30,986 youth, including 15,964 male and 15,022 female participants, covering a cumulative distance of 573 kilometres. In addition, 40,838 young individuals, comprising 19,885 male and 20,953 female participants, took the Nasha Mukt Yuva Sankalp.

The activity was implemented under the “Prevent” pillar of the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat campaign, which focuses on prevention through awareness, positive engagement and healthy lifestyle choices. By bringing together youth, educational institutions and local communities, the Health Walk/Run encouraged physical activity, positive peer engagement, discipline and sustainable outdoor habits, contributing to the broader objective of promoting physical and mental well-being among young people.

The Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Abhiyan seeks to build sustained awareness among young people about the risks associated with substance abuse and encourage them to make informed, healthy and responsible lifestyle choices. Through a series of nationwide interventions, MY Bharat and NSS are engaging youth and communities in activities centred on prevention, awareness and collective action..

2317928.title: Dr. Virendra Kumar, Shri B L Verma To Distribute Assistive Devices Among Senior Citizens On Swachh Bharat Diwas Tomorrow
2317928.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Dr. Virendra Kumar, Shri B L Verma To Distribute Assistive Devices Among Senior Citizens On Swachh Bharat Diwas Tomorrow
Dr Virendra Kumar To Lead ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ Tree Plantation Drive Under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 Campaign
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 8:16PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the Central Government’s continued commitment towards the welfare and dignity of senior citizens, Dr. Virendra Kumar, Hon’ble Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, will distribute assistive devices among senior citizens at a programme at Dr Ambedkar International Centre in National Capital here tomorrow. Shri B. L. Verma, Hon’ble Minister of State of Social Justice and Empowerment, will also grace the occasion.

A Senior Official in the Ministry informed that under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY), 114 senior citizens residing in Senior Citizens’ Homes in New Delhi and the National Capital Region will receive a total of 662 assistive devices and aids costing over ₹10 lakh, free of cost. The devices have been identified according to the individual needs of the beneficiaries through assessment camps conducted in September 2026.

The assistive devices include folding wheelchairs and commode wheelchairs, crutches, walking sticks, BTE hearing aids, spinal supports, walkers, cervical collars, chairs with commode, knee braces, LS belts, tripods/tetrapods and silicone foam cushions.

The initiative reflects the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment’s continued commitment to enabling senior citizens to live with dignity, good health and independence.

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment is the nodal department for the welfare of senior citizens in the country. Its Senior Citizens Division formulates and implements policies and programmes for the elderly in close collaboration with State Governments, Non-Governmental Organisations and civil society. The Division administers the umbrella scheme Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), and the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana is a key component.

The Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana is implemented by the Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO), a Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. The distribution of assistive devices is in consonance with the Government’s vision of Viksit Bharat@2047, which seeks to ensure inclusive growth and enable every citizen, including senior citizens, to live with dignity, good health and independence.

Under the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign, a tree sapling plantation drive with the theme “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” will be led by Dr. Virendra Kumar, Hon’ble Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, tomorrow on the occasion of Swachh Bharat Diwas. The plantation drive is scheduled to be held at Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation in New Delhi. The initiative will reinforce the message of environmental sustainability, cleanliness and collective responsibility, while encouraging citizens to contribute towards a greener, cleaner and healthier India.

The Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana, launched on 1st April 2017, is fully funded by the Government of India and provides free assistive devices to eligible senior citizens with age-related physical frailty.

Since its launch, more than 55 lakh assistive devices have been provided to more than 10 lakh senior citizens across the country, with about 45 per cent of the beneficiaries being women. 109 Pradhan Mantri Divyasha Vayoshri Kendras (PMD-VKs) are operational across the country so far.

The initiatives reflect the Government’s commitment to inclusive development, dignity of senior citizens, environmental sustainability and Jan Bhagidari, contributing towards the broader vision of Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

2317919.title: Union Minister of State (I/C) for Law and Justice Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal Leads Cleanliness Initiative; Officers and Officials Participate in Collective Effort for Cleaner and Sustainable Environment.
2317919.body_html:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Union Minister of State (I/C) for Law and Justice Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal Leads Cleanliness Initiative; Officers and Officials Participate in Collective Effort for Cleaner and Sustainable Environment.
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 8:07PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the Special Campaign 6 and Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026, the Department of Legal Affairs and the Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, organised a Shramdaan at the historic Safdarjung Tomb, New Delhi, on 01 October 2026. The initiative aimed at promoting the spirit of cleanliness, civic responsibility and community participation, while reinforcing the importance of collective efforts towards  cleaner public places and promoting sustainable environment.

The Shramdaan was conducted under the leadership of Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Hon’ble Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice. Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Department of Legal Affairs and Legislative Department, along with senior officers and officials of both the Departments and learned Law Officers actively participated. The event witnessed active participation of the Panel Counsels of Union of India led by Shri Chetan Sharma, the Ld. ASG, Delhi High Court.

The participation of the Departments in the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign reflects the Government’s emphasis on Jan Bhagidari and on transforming cleanliness from a periodic activity into a sustained public habit. Through their active participation in the cleanliness drive, officers and officials reaffirmed that maintaining clean surroundings is a collective responsibility that requires the involvement of institutions as well as citizens.

The Shramdaan event provided an opportunity for officers and officials to participate directly in the cleanliness of historic tourist centre and to reinforce the message that Shramdaan is an expression of collective ownership, dignity of labour and responsible citizenship.

Speaking on the occasion, the Hon’ble Minister highlighted the importance of collective participation in the Swachhata movement and encouraged everyone to make cleanliness an integral part of everyday life. He emphasised that sustained efforts by individual and institutions are essential for creating cleaner surroundings and promoting a healthy and sustainable environment. He highlighted the coinciding of the event with the International Day of Older Persons Celebrated Globally on October 1, 2026 and felicitated the senior most person in the gathering who is a panel advocate for the Union of India at Delhi High Court.

Under the pillar of the campaign, Hon’ble Minister also presented Swachhata kits to the Safai Karamcharis of the Ministry recognising their efforts and value of work.

The Shramdaan was part of the Department’s continued participation in Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, reaffirming its commitment to cleanliness, sanitation, environmental awareness and responsible resource management. The campaign provides an important platform for government organisations and citizens to come together and contribute towards improving public spaces through collective action.

2317915.title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Participates in Opening Day of G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwauke, U.S
2317915.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Participates in Opening Day of G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwauke, U.S
Shri Piyush Goyal Highlights India’s Food Security Measures and Reaffirms Commitment to Rules-Based Multilateral Trading System
G20 Trade Ministers Reach Consensus on Statement on Weaponization of Food through Coercive Trade Actions
Shri Piyush Goyal Holds Bilateral Meetings with Trade Ministers and Representatives of Key G20 Partners on Sidelines of G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 7:59PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal participated in the opening day of the G20 Trade Ministers’ Meeting in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, hosted under the United States G20 Presidency.

Speaking at the session on food and trade, Shri Goyal thanked the Presidency for placing food at the centre of the discussions. He said that ensuring food security for all and creating greater opportunities for farmers are central to India’s policy and reiterated that food must never be used as an instrument of pressure against any country. He said that countries of the Global South are among the most adversely impacted by the food, fuel and fertiliser crises caused by global conflicts, and stressed that today’s fertiliser shortage could become tomorrow’s food crisis.

Shri Goyal said that during the COVID-19 pandemic, India ensured food security for over 1.4 billion citizens and supplied foodgrains to several countries in need. He noted that over 800 million people in India are currently being provided foodgrains free of cost.

The Minister said that India maintains public stockholding, procures from small and marginal farmers and, in the event of a harvest shortfall, adopts temporary and transparent measures to ensure the availability and affordability of food. He said these measures are recognised under the WTO, including through the Bali Ministerial Decision and the Geneva Ministerial Declaration. He called for a clear distinction between measures taken to ensure food security and coercive trade actions.

Shri Goyal also referred to existing mechanisms, including the G20 Agricultural Market Information System, established in 2011, and the exemption of purchases by the World Food Programme from export restrictions, adopted at the 12th Ministerial Conference of the WTO. He reaffirmed India’s commitment to a rules-based, fair, non-discriminatory, equitable, transparent, open, inclusive and multilateral trading system, with the WTO at its core.

The Ministers reached consensus on the outcome document, ‘G20 Statement on the Weaponization of Food through Coercive Trade Actions’, and expressed their intent to continue cooperation on the subject.

Earlier in the day, Shri Goyal joined G20 Trade Ministers and Ambassador Jamieson Greer, United States Trade Representative, on a visit to the Rockwell Automation office and factory in Mequon, Wisconsin.

On the sidelines of the Meeting, Shri Goyal held bilateral meetings with the Minister of Development, Industry, Trade and Services and the Foreign Minister of Brazil; the United States Trade Representative; the European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security; the Secretary of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and President of the Board of Trade of the United Kingdom; the Secretary of Economy of Mexico; and the Minister of Finance and Economy of the Republic of Poland.
The Minister also attended the welcome dinner hosted by Ambassador Greer and Secretary Rollins of the United States Department of Agriculture at the Milwaukee Art Museum.

 

***

2317909.title: National-Level SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir Reaches Over 3.69 Lakh Beneficiaries Across 3,870 ULBs
2317909.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
National-Level SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir Reaches Over 3.69 Lakh Beneficiaries Across 3,870 ULBs
Shivir Facilitates Over 3.02 Lakh Health Check-ups, 2.24 Lakh NAMASTE Card Downloads and Distribution of 1.28 Lakh PPE Kits to SafaiMitras
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 7:45PM by PIB Delhi

Over 3,800 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), Rural Local Bodies (RLBs) and line departments participated in a national-level SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir in hybrid mode with participation from across the country, in the National Capital here.

The programme was also conducted physically at participating locations, bringing various health, safety, welfare and social protection services directly to SafaiMitras and sanitation workers.

A Senior Official in the Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment said that enthusiastic participation was witnessed from States including Meghalaya, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, Kerala and Bihar, which organised health camps across their major municipal corporations as part of the Shivir.

 

He said the proactive involvement of the States helped bring health check-ups and related services directly to SafaiMitras and sanitation workers in their respective cities, who regularly face occupational health hazards in the course of their work.

The Official said the SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir underscores the Government's commitment towards building a safer, healthier and more dignified sanitation ecosystem, while recognising the vital contribution of SafaiMitras and strengthening their access to welfare, social security and health protection measures.

 

The Official further said the Shivir witnessed extensive participation across the country, with 3,69,469 beneficiaries attending the programme. He added that as part of the initiative, 3,02,958 health check-ups were facilitated, providing sanitation workers with access to essential health services.

The Ministry Official added that a total of 2,24,521 NAMASTE Cards were downloaded by beneficiaries, while 57,967 Ayushman Cards were distributed to facilitate access to healthcare and social protection benefits.

The Official said the Shivir also facilitated 1,53,253 registrations under various Government schemes, enabling beneficiaries to connect with welfare and social security measures.

He said in a significant step towards strengthening occupational safety, 1,28,928 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kits were distributed among SafaiMitras across participating locations.

The Shivir was organised to recognise and honour the contribution of SafaiMitras and sanitation workers and to facilitate their access to health, safety, welfare and social protection measures.

 

The initiative brought multiple services together at the local level, enabling sanitation workers to access healthcare, safety equipment, Government schemes and social protection benefits through a common platform.

The extensive participation and achievements of the Shivir reaffirm the importance of coordinated efforts by the Central Government, State Governments, Urban and Rural Local Bodies and line departments in ensuring the last-mile delivery of healthcare, safety, welfare and social protection measures to sanitation workers.

2317906.title: Agreement Signed between DBN (Digital Bharat Nidhi) - Department of Telecommunications; Government of Maharashtra; MDIL; BSNL & MahaIT for Implementation of Amended BharatNet Program in Maharashtra
2317906.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
 Agreement Signed between DBN (Digital Bharat Nidhi) - Department of Telecommunications; Government of Maharashtra; MDIL; BSNL & MahaIT for Implementation of Amended BharatNet Program in Maharashtra
₹10,520 Crore Financial Support Approved for Rollout of Amended BharatNet Program in Maharashtra
Amended BharatNet Program in Maharashtra to Cover 28,237 Gram Panchayats and Provide On-Demand Connectivity to 15,799 Villages
Partnership to Strengthen and Upgrade Rural Telecom Infrastructure across Maharashtra
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 7:44PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening digital infrastructure and accelerating broadband connectivity across rural Maharashtra, Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) under Department of Telecommunications (DoT) signed an Agreement for implementation of the Amended BharatNet Program (ABP) in the State under the State-led model today at Sanchar Bhawan, New Delhi.

The Agreement was signed between Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN), DoT; Government of Maharashtra; MahaNet Digital Infrastructure Limited (MDIL); Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) and Maharashtra Information Technology Corporation Limited (MahaIT) for implementation of the Amended BharatNet Program in the State of Maharashtra.

The Agreement signing ceremony was held in the august presence of Shri Shyamal Misra, Administrator, Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN); Shri Virendra Singh, Secretary, Department of Electronics, Information Technology & Artificial Intelligence, Government of Maharashtra; Smt. Buveneswari S., MD, Maharashtra Information Technology Corporation Limited (MahaIT); Shri Papa Sudhakara Rao, Director (Enterprise Business - EB), Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL); Shri Dinesh Kumar Garg, DDG (ABP Implementation-I), Department of Telecommunications, along with senior officers of DoT, DBN and BSNL.

The signing of the Agreement marks an important milestone towards expeditious implementation of the Program and reflects the shared commitment of the Central Government and the Government of Maharashtra towards strengthening rural digital infrastructure, enhancing last-mile connectivity and promoting inclusive digital growth.

The Union Cabinet had approved the Amended BharatNet Program on 4th August 2023 with the objective of upgrading, consolidating and expanding the existing BharatNet network to ensure robust and future-ready broadband connectivity to all Gram Panchayats and villages on demand basis.

Under the Amended BharatNet Program in Maharashtra, the project will be implemented through MahaNet Digital Infrastructure Limited (MDIL). The Program will have a total scope of 28,237 Gram Panchayats, which includes upgradation of 15,171 Phase I Gram Panchayats from linear to ring topology to enhance network resilience, coverage of 12,740 Phase II Gram Panchayats, and inclusion of 326 newly created Gram Panchayats. In addition, 15,799 villages will be provided connectivity on a demand basis to strengthen last-mile connectivity.

The Government of India has approved financial support of ₹10,520 crore for implementation of the Program in Maharashtra. The initiative is expected to facilitate more than nine lakh rural home fibre connections with financial support from the Government of India and significantly enhance delivery of digital services including e-Governance, online education, telemedicine, digital payments and citizen-centric services across rural and remote areas of the State.

The Agreement signed today is expected to accelerate execution of the Program in Maharashtra and further advance the vision of a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.

About Digital Bharat Nidhi

Digital Bharat Nidhi (erstwhile USOF) was established under the Indian Telegraph (Amendment) Act, 2003 w.e.f. 01.04.2002. As per ‘The Telecommunications Act, 2023’ the Universal Service Obligation Fund, has become the Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN). The DBN has mandate to support universal service through promoting access and delivery of telecommunication service in underserved rural, remote and urban areas. It is an attached office of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications.

In order to achieve objectives of DBN, it covers various schemes and projects including BharatNet, 4G Saturation Project, Provision of Mobile Service in uncovered areas of Aspirational Districts, Mobile Services in Left Wing Extremist Areas, Mobile Services in Himalayan and Border areas, Mobile Services in Islands and Mobile Services in North Eastern Areas.

2317895.title: NHRC, India takes suomotu cognizance of report on 12-member Uttar Pradesh family allegedly kept as bonded labourers for nearly a year at a construction facility in Medchal-Malkajgiri district, Telangana
2317895.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suomotu cognizance of report on 12-member Uttar Pradesh family allegedly kept as bonded labourers for nearly a year at a construction facility in Medchal-Malkajgiri district, Telangana
Reportedly, the rescued bonded labourers lived in hazardous and unsanitary conditions, denied proper wages and subjected to abuse and movement restrictions
The Commission issues notices to the Telangana Chief Secretary, Director General of Police, Medchal-Malkajgiri District Magistrate and Cyberabad Commissioner of Police
Status of 12 rescued victims, investigation, release certificates, financial assistance and long-term rehabilitation plan sought
The Commission directs Medchal-Malkajgiri District Magistrate to take time-bound, victim-centric action 
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 7:32PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suomotu cognizance of a media report regarding a 12-member family from Uttar Pradesh, who were allegedly kept as bonded labourers for nearly a year at a construction facility in Bachupally, Medchal-Malkajgiri district, Hyderabad, Telangana. When rescued, they were reportedly found being paid meagre wages and made to work seven days a week, facing physical and verbal abuse while living in hazardous and unsanitary conditions.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise a serious issue of violation of the human rights of the labourers. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Telangana Chief Secretary, Director General of Police, Medchal-Malkajgiri District Magistrate and Cyberabad Commissioner of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within four weeks.

The report is expected to include the status and whereabouts of all 12 rescued victims and the steps taken for their immediate safety, shelter, food and medical care. It shall also include details of the FIR registered against the employer and any other responsible persons, along with the status of the investigation. The Commission also directed the Medchal-Malkajgiri District Magistrate to ensure that the entire process of release and rehabilitation is conducted in a time-bound and victim-centric manner.

The report sought from the authorities is also expected to include confirmation of the issuance of Bonded Labour Release Certificates to all eligible victims and provide details of the immediate financial assistance of up to Rs. 30,000 paid to each victim under the Central Sector Scheme for the Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourers, 2021. It shall further include a comprehensive plan for the long-term rehabilitation of the victims, including their repatriation to Uttar Pradesh, if they so desire, in coordination with the authorities in the State.

According to the media report, carried on 30th September 2026, the movement of the bonded labourers was restricted and their belongings were locked away by a supervisor. They were rescued by Revenue and Labour officials following a complaint by social workers.

2317889.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Hon’ble MoS Shri B. L. Verma Leads Shramdaan Activity under “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath” Theme in Delhi
Shramdaan Activity Reaffirms Commitment to Jan Bhagidari and the Vision of Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 7:28PM by PIB Delhi

As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 campaign, a Shramdaan activity was organised at the Mahila Imdad Committee (MIC), Paharganj area in National Capital here today under the leadership of Shri B. L. Verma, Hon’ble Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, in line with the campaign theme “Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath.”

Shri Verma actively participated in the Shramdaan activity and led the cleanliness activities at the premises.

He briefed the participants about the Swachh Bharat Mission, which was launched by Shri Narendra Modi, Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, on October 2, 2014, as a national movement across the length and breadth of the country. He also highlighted the achievements made under the movement.

Emphasising the importance of Jan Bhagidari in sustaining the momentum of the cleanliness movement, Shri Verma appealed to everyone to make Swachhata an integral part of their daily routine.

 

He called upon citizens to collectively contribute towards keeping their homes, workplaces and public spaces clean, reinforcing the spirit of shared responsibility and participation.

Officers of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and the Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO) also actively participated in the Shramdaan activity.

The participants collectively undertook cleanliness and sanitation activities at and around the premises, reaffirming their commitment to the spirit of Jan Bhagidari.

The Shramdaan activity reflects the Ministry’s commitment to the objectives of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 and the broader vision of a Swachh Bharat and Viksit Bharat. The initiative further underscores the importance of collective participation in making cleanliness a sustained public movement and an integral part of everyday life.

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to support initiatives that promote cleanliness, public participation and collective responsibility.

The Shramdaan activity under the Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath theme reinforces the message that sustained cleanliness can be achieved through active participation and shared commitment towards a cleaner and more developed India.

2317884.title: Special Campaign 6 : Strengthening Efficiency, Cleanliness and Citizen-Centric Service Delivery
2317884.body_html:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Special Campaign 6 : Strengthening Efficiency, Cleanliness and Citizen-Centric Service Delivery
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 7:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Labour and Employment is implementing Special Campaign 6 with a focused approach towards the timely disposal of pending matters, improved cleanliness and space management, administrative efficiency, and citizen-centric service delivery. The campaign aims to expedite the resolution of long-pending matters, including references from Members of Parliament (MPs), State Governments, inter-ministerial communications, Parliamentary Assurances, references from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), and public grievances. It seeks to streamline administrative processes, reduce pendency, and facilitate quicker disposal of matters in the interest of citizens.

The campaign also includes a comprehensive review of existing rules, regulations, and procedures to identify and eliminate unnecessary compliance requirements, simplify processes, and promote a more efficient and citizen-friendly regulatory framework.

A key focus is improving cleanliness and space utilization across the Ministry, its attached and subordinate offices, and autonomous bodies. Efforts are being undertaken to reduce clutter, optimize available space, and create clean, organized, and productive workplaces. Special emphasis is also being placed on the proper collection, segregation, and disposal of e-waste in accordance with applicable environmental norms.

During the Preparatory Phase (15–30 September 2026), the Ministry set key targets, including reviewing and organizing more than one lakh physical files, undertaking cleanliness and space-clearing activities at over 2,000 sites nationwide to create more than one lakh square feet of usable space and disposing off more than 30,000 Public Grievances & more than 5000 Grievances Appeals.

With the commencement of the Implementation Phase (2–31 October 2026), the Ministry will build upon the progress achieved during the Preparatory Phase. Concerted efforts will continue towards achieving the identified targets, reducing pendency, improving workplace conditions, streamlining processes, and strengthening efficient and citizen-centric service delivery.

2317882.title: Ministry of Tourism organises cleanliness drive under Swachhta Hi Seva Campaign
2317882.body_html:
Ministry of Tourism
Ministry of Tourism organises cleanliness drive under Swachhta Hi Seva Campaign
Around 500 participants join ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’ Shramdaan initiative at Hauz Khas Fort
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 7:19PM by PIB Delhi

Reaffirming its commitment to the Swachh Bharat Mission, the Ministry of Tourism organised a major cleanliness drive at the historic Hauz Khas Fort, New Delhi, today under the Swachhta Hi Seva Campaign. The drive was organised as part of the nationwide Shramdaan initiative, ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’, encouraging people across the country to come together and contribute their time towards cleanliness.

The drive was spearheaded by Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism, along with senior officials and staff of the Ministry. Around 500 people participated in the cleanliness and awareness activities at the heritage site.

Students and faculty members from leading hospitality and tourism management institutes also participated in the drive, including the Institute of Hotel Management (IHM), Pusa; Indian Culinary Institute (ICI), Noida; National Council for Hotel Management and Catering Technology (NCHMCT); Indian Institute of Tourism and Travel Management (IITTM), Noida; and Ashok Institute of Hotel Management (Ashok IHM).

Through the initiative, participants highlighted the importance of hygiene, civic responsibility and preservation of India’s cultural heritage. The drive sought to raise public awareness about maintaining cleanliness at tourism destinations and ensuring that the country’s iconic monuments remain clean, well-maintained and welcoming for visitors from India and across the world.

As part of the programme, students of IHM Pusa presented a short play highlighting the importance of making cleanliness a part of everyday life and contributing towards cleaner and more welcoming tourist destinations.

Ahead of the main drive, the Ministry had organised a special Felicitation Programme on 23 September 2026 to honour Safai Mitras for their contribution towards maintaining sanitation standards. The Ministry also organised a cleanliness drive at Safdarjung Tomb, New Delhi, on World Tourism Day on 27 September 2026, to spread the message of maintaining cleanliness at tourist sites.

“On behalf of all citizens, I pay my respectful tribute to the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi on his 157th birth anniversary celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti.

Gandhiji’s life and ideals are widely respected by the global community. Today, an atmosphere of war and conflict prevails in many parts of the world, affecting all nations. In these circumstances, Mahatma Gandhi’s message of peace and non-violence becomes even more relevant.

Our country is advancing towards the national goal of becoming Viksit Bharat by the year 2047. In this journey, priority is being given to the values ​​of empathy and inclusion to ensure that no citizen is deprived of the benefits of development. This vision reflects the spirit of Mahatma Gandhi’s ideal of ‘Sarvodaya’, based on the principle of the welfare and upliftment of all.

On the auspicious occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, let us reaffirm our commitment to building an empowered, developed and Atmanirbhar Bharat through our ethical conduct and active participation”.

2317859.title: High-Level Jordanian Delegation Meets Secretary (Textiles) in New Delhi
2317859.body_html:
Ministry of Textiles
High-Level Jordanian Delegation Meets Secretary (Textiles) in New Delhi
India and Jordan Discuss Strengthening Cooperation in Textiles and Apparel Sector
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 6:46PM by PIB Delhi

A high-level delegation from the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, led by H.E. Mr. Zaher Al Qatarneh, Secretary-General, Ministry of Investment, met Ms. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary (Textiles), Government of India, at the Ministry of Textiles, New Delhi, today to discuss avenues for strengthening bilateral cooperation in textiles and apparel sector.

The Jordanian delegation included H.E. Mr. Yousef Abdelghani, Ambassador of Jordan to India; Ms. Haya Iman, Director of Investment Promotion; and Ms. Noor Murad, Investment Promotion Officer. Senior officials from the Ministry of Textiles and the Ministry of External Affairs, along with representatives of the textile industry, also participated in the meeting.

The discussions focused on expanding bilateral trade, sourcing, investment and industry partnerships including Joint Ventures in the sector. Jordan’s textile and apparel imports from the world stood at around USD 2 billion in 2025, while India’s exports to Jordan were around USD 48 million, accounting for a 2.4% share and making India Jordan’s fourth-largest supplier.

The Indian side highlighted the potential for enhanced cooperation in apparels, fabrics, technical textiles, cotton textiles and made-ups, including opportunities for greater sourcing, investment and industry partnerships.

The two sides also explored opportunities for strengthening institutional and knowledge partnerships between leading fashion, design and textile institutions in India and Jordan, including student and faculty exchanges, design innovation and cooperation in AI-enabled fashion forecasting.

Both sides also discussed the possibility of reinvigorating the established institutional mechanism  to facilitate structured and sustained engagement and follow-up on identified areas of cooperation in textiles & apparel.

The meeting concluded on a positive note, with both sides agreeing to bilaterally engage and take forward the areas of cooperation identified during the discussions.

2317856.title: Union Jal Shakti Minister Shri C. R. Paatil Hosts Water Warriors from Across India at His Residence
2317856.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Union Jal Shakti Minister Shri C. R. Paatil Hosts Water Warriors from Across India at His Residence
Grassroots champions share inspiring stories of river rejuvenation, water conservation and community mobilization
Shri Paatil calls for focused action, measurable outcomes and wider Jan Bhagidari
Secretary, DoWR, RD & GR Smt. Archana Varma lauds their role in mobilising communities for collective action on water
Posted On: 01 OCT 2026 6:42PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Jal Shakti Shri C. R. Paatil today interacted with Water Conservation Warriors and River Rejuvenation Warriors from different parts of the country who have been leading grassroots initiatives in water conservation, river and water-body rejuvenation and environmental protection. The interaction, organised by the National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG) under Namami Gange, provided a platform for these grassroots champions to share their journeys, learn from one another and discuss how successful community-led models can be strengthened and replicated across the country.

The participants shared first-hand experiences of restoring rivers and ponds, undertaking Shramdaan, promoting rainwater harvesting, removing plastic and other waste near water bodies, carrying out plantation drives and mobilising women, youth, volunteers and local communities. Their stories highlighted how individual initiative, when combined with collective action and community ownership, can translate into visible and sustained improvements on the ground.

Among those who shared their work was Ramveer Tanwar, popularly known as the ‘Pondman of India’, who spoke about rejuvenating more than 100 ponds and establishing 10 mini urban forests. Kamini Kumari from Bihar highlighted her initiative in mobilising 500 women to construct 500 groundwater recharge pits along the Baya River in a single day, linking water conservation with groundwater recharge, sustainable agriculture and livelihood opportunities for women.

Surendra Singh Chaudhary, popularly known as ‘Bittu Tabahi’, shared his journey of taking up the clean-up of the polluted Ajnar River at Biaora in Rajgarh district of Madhya Pradesh. A young B.Sc. student, he began the effort on 26 January 2026 and undertook hands-on removal of plastic, weeds, sludge and other waste from the river, largely through his own initiative. His work, which began as a local effort, drew wider public attention and has inspired greater participation in the cleaning and restoration of local water bodies.

Anand Malligavad from Bengaluru spoke about his work in restoring 33 lakes and planting more than one lakh native trees. Jagdish Singh Negi from Uttarakhand shared his work in water conservation, forest restoration and converting plastic waste into eco-bricks. Subham Kumar highlighted the role of youth and volunteers in river cleanliness and his efforts to mobilise communities to remove more than 2.47 lakh kilograms of waste from the banks of the Ganga and its tributaries.

The interaction also highlighted the role of water volunteers and community groups in sustaining clean rivers and ghats. Akash Yadav from Uttar Pradesh shared how his 15-member volunteer group has contributed to the rejuvenation of four Ganga ghats and the removal of more than one tonne of plastic waste. Dr. Sanjivini Sharma from Kanpur spoke about mobilising more than 900 volunteers for Ganga conservation campaigns and removing over 120 metric tonnes of waste, besides promoting plastic recycling, reuse of discarded materials and livelihood opportunities for women through community-led waste management.

The other water warriors included Ms. Kusum Gildiyal, Sh. Jagdish Negi, Ms. Rama Tiwari, Dr. Suman Pandey, Ms. Kumari Sunita Singh, Sh. Sanjay Kumar Singh, Sh. Ajay Kumar Tivare, Sh. Nitish Kumar Singh, Sh. Kamlesh Bhai Shastri, Sh. Sandeep Chaudhary, Ms. Sirkunwar, Ms. Phoolbati and Sh. Vivek Bhat. The work of these warriors were highly appreciated by Hon’ble Minister Jal Shakti.

Addressing the gathering, Smt. Archana Varma, Secretary, Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, appreciated the role played by the Water Warriors in taking the message of water conservation and cleanliness beyond government programmes and into communities. She praised their ability to bring people together and mobilise collective action around rivers, ponds and other water bodies, and emphasised that such citizen-led participation is essential for sustaining water conservation and river rejuvenation efforts over the long term.

Addressing the participants, Shri C. R. Paatil congratulated them for their commitment and said that listening directly to their experiences was an opportunity to understand the scale, diversity and impact of grassroots action taking place across the country. He acknowledged that many of them had worked through difficult local circumstances and had nevertheless succeeded in bringing people together for the protection of water and the environment. Referring to the larger national movement, Shri Paatil said that under the visionary leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, water conservation has evolved into a nationwide Jan Andolan anchored in Jan Bhagidari. He said that the Prime Minister's consistent emphasis on conserving every drop of water has inspired citizens and communities across the country to take ownership of water conservation, and that the work of the Water Warriors and reflects this spirit of collective action.

The Minister emphasized that the next step should be to translate this energy into focused, measurable and sustained outcomes. He encouraged the participants to identify specific rivers, ponds, ghats and other water bodies, set clear targets and demonstrate visible improvement on the ground. He also stressed the importance of involving women, youth, schoolchildren, senior citizens and other sections of society so that water conservation and cleanliness become enduring people’s movements rather than one-time activities.

Shri Paatil encouraged the Water Warriors to remain connected with one another, regularly share their work and learn from successful models being implemented in different parts of the country. He said that good local initiatives should not remain confined to one place, but should be adapted and expanded wherever they can help communities address similar challenges.

The Water Warriors expressed happiness at being invited by the Minister to his residence and at the opportunity to share their stories directly with him. They also valued the chance to interact with fellow grassroots champions from different parts of India, exchange experiences, understand different approaches to community mobilisation and explore ways to remain connected and collaborate in future.

The interaction reaffirmed that protecting rivers and conserving water cannot be achieved through infrastructure and government programmes alone. Sustained Jan Bhagidari, Shramdaan, responsible community behaviour and committed grassroots leadership are equally important. The experiences shared during the meeting demonstrated how citizens, volunteers and local communities can become powerful partners in the national effort for clean rivers, conserved water resources and a cleaner, more sustainable environment.

***
